intuition.title: Two concentrations and two composition bases
intuition.text: The target is 8 mol% Sc2O3-stabilized zirconia on an oxide basis. The method separately prints nominal starting values of 92 mol% ZrO(NO3)2 and 16 mol% Sc(NO3)3. Those literal feed values are not two normalized percentages summing to 100, nor an 8 mol% scandium-cation fraction. Total cation concentration is separate from urea concentration. The stock solvent and individual nitrate charges are not specified.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1, Experimental Procedure

intuition.title: Aging changes phase formation
intuition.text: The authors attribute the low-temperature stage to slow urea hydrolysis and homogeneous co-precipitation before crystallization at 180 °C. They propose polymeric/hydrous-oxide intermediates and a more ordered precursor; these are mechanistic interpretations, not measured transient species or molecular structures. Direct 180 °C treatment gives more monoclinic phase.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Results and Discussion; Figure 2

intuition.title: The 0.5 mol/L boundary remains unresolved
intuition.text: The first-page discussion describes pure cubic material for urea ≤0.5 mol/L. The conclusion uses <0.5 mol/L, and Figure 2a shows a small nonzero monoclinic point at 0.5 mol/L. The 0.5 mol/L route therefore retains an unresolved phase-purity boundary rather than a blanket pure-cubic label or an invented exact fraction.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–3, Results, Figure 2a and Conclusions

intuition.title: The short concentration series is a separate schedule
intuition.text: Figure 3 uses 80 °C for 24 h followed by 180 °C for 48 h, at 0.05, 0.1, 0.25 and 0.5 mol/L total cations with cation:urea = 1:4. The long urea series uses 48 h followed by 72 h. The 0.5 mol/L cation endpoint with that ratio is not silently reconciled with the general 0.1–1.5 mol/L urea range. Individual phase fractions for Figure 3 are not tabulated.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Experimental Procedure and Figure 3

intuition.title: Three size estimates describe different observables
intuition.text: For 0.05 mol/L cations and 0.2 mol/L urea after the long schedule, TEM gives an average grain size below 10 nm, XRD linewidth analysis gives 7.0 nm, and BET gives a specific surface area of 157 m²/g with an author-calculated equivalent size of 6 nm. These are separate analytical quantities, not repeated TEM diameters. Figure 5 shows a 50 nm scale bar.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Figure 5 and morphology/XRD/BET paragraph

intuition.title: Calcination retains cubic phase while promoting grain growth
intuition.text: The paper reports cubic phase retention during 1 h calcination under stagnant air over 600–1200 °C. Grain size changes little below 800 °C and grows substantially above 1000 °C, reaching a text-reported XRD crystallite size of 36.5 nm at 1200 °C. Other Figure 6 point ordinates are preserved visually without extracting exact numbers.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1, 3, Experimental Procedure, calcination paragraph and Figure 6

intuition.title: Solution pH and applications are separate scopes
intuition.text: Figure 4 shows increasing final solution pH and decreasing XRD crystallite size as urea concentration rises. The plotted pH and size ordinates are not tabulated here. The paper motivates solid-oxide fuel-cell electrolytes through cited literature but supplies no conductivity measurement for these powders.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Introduction and Figure 4

Grain size changes little below 800 °C and grows substantially above 1000 °C, reaching a text-reported XRD crystallite size of 36.5 nm at 1200 °C. Other Figure 6 point ordinates are preserved visually without extracting exact numbers.

intuition.title: Solution pH and applications are separate scopes
intuition.text: Figure 4 shows increasing final solution pH and decreasing XRD crystallite size as urea concentration rises. The plotted pH and size ordinates are not tabulated here. intuition.title: Two concentrations and two composition bases
intuition.text: The target is 8 mol% Sc2O3-stabilized zirconia on an oxide basis. The method separately prints nominal starting values of 92 mol% ZrO(NO3)2 and 16 mol% Sc(NO3)3. Those literal feed values are not two normalized percentages summing to 100, nor an 8 mol% scandium-cation fraction. Total cation concentration is separate from urea concentration. The stock solvent and individual nitrate charges are not specified.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1, Experimental Procedure

intuition.title: Aging changes phase formation
intuition.text: The authors attribute the low-temperature stage to slow urea hydrolysis and homogeneous co-precipitation before crystallization at 180 °C. They propose polymeric/hydrous-oxide intermediates and a more ordered precursor; these are mechanistic interpretations, not measured transient species or molecular structures. Direct 180 °C treatment gives more monoclinic phase.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Results and Discussion; Figure 2

intuition.title: The 0.5 mol/L boundary remains unresolved
intuition.text: The first-page discussion describes pure cubic material for urea ≤0.5 mol/L. The conclusion uses <0.5 mol/L, and Figure 2a shows a small nonzero monoclinic point at 0.5 mol/L. The 0.5 mol/L route therefore retains an unresolved phase-purity boundary rather than a blanket pure-cubic label or an invented exact fraction.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–3, Results, Figure 2a and Conclusions

intuition.title: The short concentration series is a separate schedule
intuition.text: Figure 3 uses 80 °C for 24 h followed by 180 °C for 48 h, at 0.05, 0.1, 0.25 and 0.5 mol/L total cations with cation:urea = 1:4. The long urea series uses 48 h followed by 72 h. The 0.5 mol/L cation endpoint with that ratio is not silently reconciled with the general 0.1–1.5 mol/L urea range. Individual phase fractions for Figure 3 are not tabulated.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Experimental Procedure and Figure 3

intuition.title: Three size estimates describe different observables
intuition.text: For 0.05 mol/L cations and 0.2 mol/L urea after the long schedule, TEM gives an average grain size below 10 nm, XRD linewidth analysis gives 7.0 nm, and BET gives a specific surface area of 157 m²/g with an author-calculated equivalent size of 6 nm. These are separate analytical quantities, not repeated TEM diameters. Figure 5 shows a 50 nm scale bar.

intuition.title: Two concentrations and two composition bases
intuition.text: The target is 8 mol% Sc2O3-stabilized zirconia on an oxide basis. The method separately prints nominal starting values of 92 mol% ZrO(NO3)2 and 16 mol% Sc(NO3)3. Those literal feed values are not two normalized percentages summing to 100, nor an 8 mol% scandium-cation fraction. Total cation concentration is separate from urea concentration. The stock solvent and individual nitrate charges are not specified.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1, Experimental Procedure

intuition.title: Aging changes phase formation
intuition.text: The authors attribute the low-temperature stage to slow urea hydrolysis and homogeneous co-precipitation before crystallization at 180 °C. They propose polymeric/hydrous-oxide intermediates and a more ordered precursor; these are mechanistic interpretations, not measured transient species or molecular structures. Direct 180 °C treatment gives more monoclinic phase.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Results and Discussion; Figure 2

intuition.title: The 0.5 mol/L boundary remains unresolved
intuition.text: The first-page discussion describes pure cubic material for urea ≤0.5 mol/L. The conclusion uses <0.5 mol/L, and Figure 2a shows a small nonzero monoclinic point at 0.5 mol/L. The 0.5 mol/L route therefore retains an unresolved phase-purity boundary rather than a blanket pure-cubic label or an invented exact fraction.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–3, Results, Figure 2a and Conclusions

intuition.title: The short concentration series is a separate schedule
intuition.text: Figure 3 uses 80 °C for 24 h followed by 180 °C for 48 h, at 0.05, 0.1, 0.25 and 0.5 mol/L total cations with cation:urea = 1:4. The long urea series uses 48 h followed by 72 h. The 0.5 mol/L cation endpoint with that ratio is not silently reconciled with the general 0.1–1.5 mol/L urea range. Individual phase fractions for Figure 3 are not tabulated.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Experimental Procedure and Figure 3

intuition.title: Three size estimates describe different observables
intuition.text: For 0.05 mol/L cations and 0.2 mol/L urea after the long schedule, TEM gives an average grain size below 10 nm, XRD linewidth analysis gives 7.0 nm, and BET gives a specific surface area of 157 m²/g with an author-calculated equivalent size of 6 nm. These are separate analytical quantities, not repeated TEM diameters. Figure 5 shows a 50 nm scale bar.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Figure 5 and morphology/XRD/BET paragraph

intuition.title: Calcination retains cubic phase while promoting grain growth
intuition.text: The paper reports cubic phase retention during 1 h calcination under stagnant air over 600–1200 °C. Grain size changes little below 800 °C and grows substantially above 1000 °C, reaching a text-reported XRD crystallite size of 36.5 nm at 1200 °C. Other Figure 6 point ordinates are preserved visually without extracting exact numbers.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1, 3, Experimental Procedure, calcination paragraph and Figure 6

intuition.title: Solution pH and applications are separate scopes
intuition.text: Figure 4 shows increasing final solution pH and decreasing XRD crystallite size as urea concentration rises. The plotted pH and size ordinates are not tabulated here. The paper motivates solid-oxide fuel-cell electrolytes through cited literature but supplies no conductivity measurement for these powders.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Introduction and Figure 4

intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Results and Discussion; Figure 2

intuition.title: The 0.5 mol/L boundary remains unresolved
intuition.text: The first-page discussion describes pure cubic material for urea ≤0.5 mol/L. The conclusion uses <0.5 mol/L, and Figure 2a shows a small nonzero monoclinic point at 0.5 mol/L. The 0.5 mol/L route therefore retains an unresolved phase-purity boundary rather than a blanket pure-cubic label or an invented exact fraction.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–3, Results, Figure 2a and Conclusions

intuition.title: The short concentration series is a separate schedule
intuition.text: Figure 3 uses 80 °C for 24 h followed by 180 °C for 48 h, at 0.05, 0.1, 0.25 and 0.5 mol/L total cations with cation:urea = 1:4. The long urea series uses 48 h followed by 72 h. The 0.5 mol/L cation endpoint with that ratio is not silently reconciled with the general 0.1–1.5 mol/L urea range. Individual phase fractions for Figure 3 are not tabulated.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Experimental Procedure and Figure 3

intuition.title: Three size estimates describe different observables
intuition.text: For 0.05 mol/L cations and 0.2 mol/L urea after the long schedule, TEM gives an average grain size below 10 nm, XRD linewidth analysis gives 7.0 nm, and BET gives a specific surface area of 157 m²/g with an author-calculated equivalent size of 6 nm. These are separate analytical quantities, not repeated TEM diameters. Figure 5 shows a 50 nm scale bar.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Figure 5 and morphology/XRD/BET paragraph

intuition.title: Calcination retains cubic phase while promoting grain growth
intuition.text: The paper reports cubic phase retention during 1 h calcination under stagnant air over 600–1200 °C. Grain size changes little below 800 °C and grows substantially above 1000 °C, reaching a text-reported XRD crystallite size of 36.5 nm at 1200 °C. Other Figure 6 point ordinates are preserved visually without extracting exact numbers.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1, 3, Experimental Procedure, calcination paragraph and Figure 6

intuition.title: Solution pH and applications are separate scopes
intuition.text: Figure 4 shows increasing final solution pH and decreasing XRD crystallite size as urea concentration rises. The plotted pH and size ordinates are not tabulated here. The paper motivates solid-oxide fuel-cell electrolytes through cited literature but supplies no conductivity measurement for these powders.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Introduction and Figure 4

intuition.title: Study context: Sol–gel rate and ordering
intuition.text: The authors connect acid-controlled silica condensation with film homogeneity. Extensive TEOS aging reduces ordering; BTEE aging has a weaker effect attributed to slower hydrolysis/condensation. This is source interpretation, not a quantitative rate model.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–4, Sol–gel and aging discussion

intuition.title: Study context: Two structural length scales
intuition.text: Fcc and Fm3m in the low-angle/TEM discussion concern the nanocrystal superlattice. The10.5/10.8nm values must not be used as atomic Au lattice constants. No atomic coordinates are supplied.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3–4, XRD/TEM and orientation discussion

intuition.title: Study context: Micelle-mediated compatibility
intuition.text: The source attributes aqueous stability to n-DT/CTAB chain interdigitation and assembly to charge/hydrogen-bond interactions with hydrolyzed silica. These are authors’ mechanisms, not direct surface-coordinate measurements.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Micelles and assembly interpretation

intuition.title: Study context: Unresolved variants

intuition.title: Source ligand-size statements conflict
intuition.text: The explicit Brus-model diameters are3.88 nm for ME/Cd2+=0.5,4.34 nm for 1 and 5.02 nm for 2. The text also says increasing ligand decreases size and blue-shifts absorption. Both are retained without reversing sample labels. The peak list396 nm (3.13 eV),400 nm (3.10 eV),410 nm (3.03 eV) is retained at series scope because its ordering and trend cannot safely repair that conflict.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Figure1 and ligand-ratio discussion

intuition.title: Solvent and ligand series are not a specimen crosswalk
intuition.text: The solvent-series ratios H2O/DMF=0.2,0.45 and 0.9 by mass have peaks377,388 and 400 nm and author-model diameters3.71,3.98 and 4.34 nm, respectively. Their ME amount is unspecified. Do not merge the0.2 solvent-series specimen with the2/1 ME specimen solely from matching solvent ratio. Precipitation above a1.5 mass ratio is qualitative.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Figure3 and solvent discussion

intuition.title: Phase, TEM and model estimates have different scopes
intuition.text: Figure 2 shows the2 h ME/Cd2+/S2−=2/1/0.67 specimen with about 5 nm mean TEM size. Figure 4 compares with-ME and no-ME2 h specimens and attributes overlapping peaks to cubic and hexagonal CdS; no exact phase fraction or refined unit cell is supplied. UV-derived sizes are model estimates, not TEM measurements.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Figures2–4 and corresponding discussion

intuition.title: Ligand binding and TGA labels
intuition.text: The authors infer robust ME–CdS bonding from FT-IR and TGA. They report decomposition beginning near 220 °C, pure-ME boiling point157 °C, about 25 wt% organic ME and an ambiguous statement about 95 wt% of sample beginning to decompose. Figure 5 caption says(a) without ME,(b) with ME; the body reverses those letters. Keep the numeric prose at source-context scope instead of treating95% as a measured loss or using the swapped labels.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3–4, Figure5 and TGA discussion

intuition.title: Two steps graft polyurethane
intuition.text: Hydroxyl-coated CdS is reacted with TDI at 85 °C for 3 h under nitrogen. BG/PPG in DMF and catalyst are added dropwise at 85 °C. This stage lasts 0.5 h; the addition duration is not separately reported. It is followed by 90 °C for 4 h. The overall BG:PPG:TDI ratio is 1:1:1.6. Absolute charges, the 50 wt% DMF denominator and film formation are unresolved. FT-IR supports NCO-bearing intermediates, not a measured single molecular geometry.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, 4, Polymer synthesis, Scheme1 and Figure6

intuition.title: Optical hybrid results are qualified
intuition.text: The 1.5 and 3.0 wt% CdS hybrids have absorption near 400 nm. In the Figure 7 discussion, the authors interpret this as unchanged CdS size of about 5 nm; it is not a hybrid TEM measurement. The Figure 8 discussion attributes broader hybrid PL tentatively to possible changes in CdS surface structure and particle size. These are distinct source-attributed interpretations, not resolved measurements. CdS suspension has approximate 425 and 600 nm bands with 325 nm excitation; the 1.5 wt% hybrid film has stronger, broader emission. No graph-only intensities, linewidths or quantum yields are extracted.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 4, Figures7–8 and optical discussion

intuition.title: Infrared prose and figure disagree
intuition.text: Hydroxyl-coated CdS prose gives 1105 and 1020 cm−1 (C–O),2926 and 2850 cm−1 (C–H), and 1440 cm−1 (CH2); Figure 6a labels 2960 rather than 2926 cm−1. TDI-modified CdS has 2262 cm−1 (NCO) and 1712 cm−1 (carbamate). The 2960/2926 discrepancy is preserved.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 4, Figure6 and FT-IR paragraph

intuition.title: Phase, TEM and model estimates have different scopes
intuition.text: Figure 2 shows the2 h ME/Cd2+/S2−=2/1/0.67 specimen with about 5 nm mean TEM size. Figure 4 compares with-ME and no-ME2 h specimens and attributes overlapping peaks to cubic and hexagonal CdS; no exact phase fraction or refined unit cell is supplied. UV-derived sizes are model estimates, not TEM measurements.

intuition.title: Ligand binding and TGA labels
intuition.text: The authors infer robust ME–CdS bonding from FT-IR and TGA. They report decomposition beginning near 220 °C, pure-ME boiling point157 °C, about 25 wt% organic ME and an ambiguous statement about 95 wt% of sample beginning to decompose. Figure 5 caption says(a) without ME,(b) with ME; the body reverses those letters. Keep the numeric prose at source-context scope instead of treating95% as a measured loss or using the swapped labels.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3–4, Figure5 and TGA discussion

intuition.title: Two steps graft polyurethane
intuition.text: Hydroxyl-coated CdS is reacted with TDI at 85 °C for 3 h under nitrogen. BG/PPG in DMF and catalyst are added dropwise at 85 °C. This stage lasts 0.5 h; the addition duration is not separately reported. It is followed by 90 °C for 4 h. The overall BG:PPG:TDI ratio is 1:1:1.6. Absolute charges, the 50 wt% DMF denominator and film formation are unresolved. FT-IR supports NCO-bearing intermediates, not a measured single molecular geometry.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, 4, Polymer synthesis, Scheme1 and Figure6

intuition.title: Optical hybrid results are qualified
intuition.text: The 1.5 and 3.0 wt% CdS hybrids have absorption near 400 nm. In the Figure 7 discussion, the authors interpret this as unchanged CdS size of about 5 nm; it is not a hybrid TEM measurement. The Figure 8 discussion attributes broader hybrid PL tentatively to possible changes in CdS surface structure and particle size. These are distinct source-attributed interpretations, not resolved measurements. CdS suspension has approximate 425 and 600 nm bands with 325 nm excitation; the 1.5 wt% hybrid film has stronger, broader emission. No graph-only intensities, linewidths or quantum yields are extracted.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 4, Figures7–8 and optical discussion

intuition.title: Infrared prose and figure disagree
intuition.text: Hydroxyl-coated CdS prose gives 1105 and 1020 cm−1 (C–O),2926 and 2850 cm−1 (C–H), and 1440 cm−1 (CH2); Figure 6a labels 2960 rather than 2926 cm−1. TDI-modified CdS has 2262 cm−1 (NCO) and 1712 cm−1 (carbamate). The 2960/2926 discrepancy is preserved.

The peak list396 nm (3.13 eV),400 nm (3.10 eV),410 nm (3.03 eV) is retained at series scope because its ordering and trend cannot safely repair that conflict.

intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Figure3 and solvent discussion

intuition.title: Phase, TEM and model estimates have different scopes
intuition.text: Figure 2 shows the2 h ME/Cd2+/S2−=2/1/0.67 specimen with about 5 nm mean TEM size. Figure 4 compares with-ME and no-ME2 h specimens and attributes overlapping peaks to cubic and hexagonal CdS; no exact phase fraction or refined unit cell is supplied. UV-derived sizes are model estimates, not TEM measurements.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Figures2–4 and corresponding discussion

intuition.title: Ligand binding and TGA labels
intuition.text: The authors infer robust ME–CdS bonding from FT-IR and TGA. They report decomposition beginning near 220 °C, pure-ME boiling point157 °C, about 25 wt% organic ME and an ambiguous statement about 95 wt% of sample beginning to decompose. Figure 5 caption says(a) without ME,(b) with ME; the body reverses those letters. Keep the numeric prose at source-context scope instead of treating95% as a measured loss or using the swapped labels.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3–4, Figure5 and TGA discussion

intuition.title: Two steps graft polyurethane
intuition.text: Hydroxyl-coated CdS is reacted with TDI at 85 °C for 3 h under nitrogen. BG/PPG in DMF and catalyst are added dropwise at 85 °C. This stage lasts 0.5 h; the addition duration is not separately reported. It is followed by 90 °C for 4 h. The overall BG:PPG:TDI ratio is 1:1:1.6. Absolute charges, the 50 wt% DMF denominator and film formation are unresolved. FT-IR supports NCO-bearing intermediates, not a measured single molecular geometry.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, 4, Polymer synthesis, Scheme1 and Figure6

intuition.title: Optical hybrid results are qualified
intuition.text: The 1.5 and 3.0 wt% CdS hybrids have absorption near 400 nm. In the Figure 7 discussion, the authors interpret this as unchanged CdS size of about 5 nm; it is not a hybrid TEM measurement. The Figure 8 discussion attributes broader hybrid PL tentatively to possible changes in CdS surface structure and particle size. These are distinct source-attributed interpretations, not resolved measurements. CdS suspension has approximate 425 and 600 nm bands with 325 nm excitation; the 1.5 wt% hybrid film has stronger, broader emission. No graph-only intensities, linewidths or quantum yields are extracted.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 4, Figures7–8 and optical discussion

intuition.title: Infrared prose and figure disagree
intuition.text: Hydroxyl-coated CdS prose gives 1105 and 1020 cm−1 (C–O),2926 and 2850 cm−1 (C–H), and 1440 cm−1 (CH2); Figure 6a labels 2960 rather than 2926 cm−1. TDI-modified CdS has 2262 cm−1 (NCO) and 1712 cm−1 (carbamate). The 2960/2926 discrepancy is preserved.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 4, Figure6 and FT-IR paragraph

intuition.text: The explicit Brus-model diameters are3.88 nm for ME/Cd2+=0.5,4.34 nm for 1 and 5.02 nm for 2. The text also says increasing ligand decreases size and blue-shifts absorption. Both are retained without reversing sample labels. The peak list396 nm (3.13 eV),400 nm (3.10 eV),410 nm (3.03 eV) is retained at series scope because its ordering and trend cannot safely repair that conflict.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Figure1 and ligand-ratio discussion

intuition.title: Solvent and ligand series are not a specimen crosswalk
intuition.text: The solvent-series ratios H2O/DMF=0.2,0.45 and 0.9 by mass have peaks377,388 and 400 nm and author-model diameters3.71,3.98 and 4.34 nm, respectively. Their ME amount is unspecified. Do not merge the0.2 solvent-series specimen with the2/1 ME specimen solely from matching solvent ratio. Precipitation above a1.5 mass ratio is qualitative.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Figure3 and solvent discussion

intuition.title: Phase, TEM and model estimates have different scopes
intuition.text: Figure 2 shows the2 h ME/Cd2+/S2−=2/1/0.67 specimen with about 5 nm mean TEM size. Figure 4 compares with-ME and no-ME2 h specimens and attributes overlapping peaks to cubic and hexagonal CdS; no exact phase fraction or refined unit cell is supplied. UV-derived sizes are model estimates, not TEM measurements.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Figures2–4 and corresponding discussion

intuition.title: Ligand binding and TGA labels
intuition.text: The authors infer robust ME–CdS bonding from FT-IR and TGA. They report decomposition beginning near 220 °C, pure-ME boiling point157 °C, about 25 wt% organic ME and an ambiguous statement about 95 wt% of sample beginning to decompose. Figure 5 caption says(a) without ME,(b) with ME; the body reverses those letters. Keep the numeric prose at source-context scope instead of treating95% as a measured loss or using the swapped labels.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3–4, Figure5 and TGA discussion

intuition.title: Two steps graft polyurethane
intuition.text: Hydroxyl-coated CdS is reacted with TDI at 85 °C for 3 h under nitrogen. BG/PPG in DMF and catalyst are added dropwise at 85 °C. This stage lasts 0.5 h; the addition duration is not separately reported. It is followed by 90 °C for 4 h. The overall BG:PPG:TDI ratio is 1:1:1.6. Absolute charges, the 50 wt% DMF denominator and film formation are unresolved. FT-IR supports NCO-bearing intermediates, not a measured single molecular geometry.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, 4, Polymer synthesis, Scheme1 and Figure6

intuition.title: Optical hybrid results are qualified
intuition.text: The 1.5 and 3.0 wt% CdS hybrids have absorption near 400 nm. In the Figure 7 discussion, the authors interpret this as unchanged CdS size of about 5 nm; it is not a hybrid TEM measurement. The Figure 8 discussion attributes broader hybrid PL tentatively to possible changes in CdS surface structure and particle size. These are distinct source-attributed interpretations, not resolved measurements. CdS suspension has approximate 425 and 600 nm bands with 325 nm excitation; the 1.5 wt% hybrid film has stronger, broader emission. No graph-only intensities, linewidths or quantum yields are extracted.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 4, Figures7–8 and optical discussion

intuition.title: Infrared prose and figure disagree
intuition.text: Hydroxyl-coated CdS prose gives 1105 and 1020 cm−1 (C–O),2926 and 2850 cm−1 (C–H), and 1440 cm−1 (CH2); Figure 6a labels 2960 rather than 2926 cm−1. TDI-modified CdS has 2262 cm−1 (NCO) and 1712 cm−1 (carbamate). The 2960/2926 discrepancy is preserved.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 4, Figure6 and FT-IR paragraph

intuition.title: Phase, TEM and model estimates have different scopes
intuition.text: Figure 2 shows the2 h ME/Cd2+/S2−=2/1/0.67 specimen with about 5 nm mean TEM size. Figure 4 compares with-ME and no-ME2 h specimens and attributes overlapping peaks to cubic and hexagonal CdS; no exact phase fraction or refined unit cell is supplied. UV-derived sizes are model estimates, not TEM measurements.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Figures2–4 and corresponding discussion

intuition.title: Ligand binding and TGA labels
intuition.text: The authors infer robust ME–CdS bonding from FT-IR and TGA. They report decomposition beginning near 220 °C, pure-ME boiling point157 °C, about 25 wt% organic ME and an ambiguous statement about 95 wt% of sample beginning to decompose. Figure 5 caption says(a) without ME,(b) with ME; the body reverses those letters. Keep the numeric prose at source-context scope instead of treating95% as a measured loss or using the swapped labels.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3–4, Figure5 and TGA discussion

intuition.title: Two steps graft polyurethane
intuition.text: Hydroxyl-coated CdS is reacted with TDI at 85 °C for 3 h under nitrogen. BG/PPG in DMF and catalyst are added dropwise at 85 °C. This stage lasts 0.5 h; the addition duration is not separately reported. It is followed by 90 °C for 4 h. The overall BG:PPG:TDI ratio is 1:1:1.6. Absolute charges, the 50 wt% DMF denominator and film formation are unresolved. FT-IR supports NCO-bearing intermediates, not a measured single molecular geometry.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, 4, Polymer synthesis, Scheme1 and Figure6

intuition.title: Optical hybrid results are qualified
intuition.text: The 1.5 and 3.0 wt% CdS hybrids have absorption near 400 nm. In the Figure 7 discussion, the authors interpret this as unchanged CdS size of about 5 nm; it is not a hybrid TEM measurement. The Figure 8 discussion attributes broader hybrid PL tentatively to possible changes in CdS surface structure and particle size. These are distinct source-attributed interpretations, not resolved measurements. CdS suspension has approximate 425 and 600 nm bands with 325 nm excitation; the 1.5 wt% hybrid film has stronger, broader emission. No graph-only intensities, linewidths or quantum yields are extracted.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 4, Figures7–8 and optical discussion

intuition.title: Infrared prose and figure disagree
intuition.text: Hydroxyl-coated CdS prose gives 1105 and 1020 cm−1 (C–O),2926 and 2850 cm−1 (C–H), and 1440 cm−1 (CH2); Figure 6a labels 2960 rather than 2926 cm−1. TDI-modified CdS has 2262 cm−1 (NCO) and 1712 cm−1 (carbamate). The 2960/2926 discrepancy is preserved.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 4, Figure6 and FT-IR paragraph

intuition.title: Phase, TEM and model estimates have different scopes
intuition.text: Figure 2 shows the2 h ME/Cd2+/S2−=2/1/0.67 specimen with about 5 nm mean TEM size. Figure 4 compares with-ME and no-ME2 h specimens and attributes overlapping peaks to cubic and hexagonal CdS; no exact phase fraction or refined unit cell is supplied. UV-derived sizes are model estimates, not TEM measurements.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Figures2–4 and corresponding discussion

intuition.title: Ligand binding and TGA labels
intuition.text: The authors infer robust ME–CdS bonding from FT-IR and TGA. They report decomposition beginning near 220 °C, pure-ME boiling point157 °C, about 25 wt% organic ME and an ambiguous statement about 95 wt% of sample beginning to decompose. Figure 5 caption says(a) without ME,(b) with ME; the body reverses those letters. Keep the numeric prose at source-context scope instead of treating95% as a measured loss or using the swapped labels.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3–4, Figure5 and TGA discussion

intuition.title: Two steps graft polyurethane
intuition.text: Hydroxyl-coated CdS is reacted with TDI at 85 °C for 3 h under nitrogen. BG/PPG in DMF and catalyst are added dropwise at 85 °C. This stage lasts 0.5 h; the addition duration is not separately reported. It is followed by 90 °C for 4 h. The overall BG:PPG:TDI ratio is 1:1:1.6. Absolute charges, the 50 wt% DMF denominator and film formation are unresolved. FT-IR supports NCO-bearing intermediates, not a measured single molecular geometry.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, 4, Polymer synthesis, Scheme1 and Figure6

intuition.title: Optical hybrid results are qualified
intuition.text: The 1.5 and 3.0 wt% CdS hybrids have absorption near 400 nm. In the Figure 7 discussion, the authors interpret this as unchanged CdS size of about 5 nm; it is not a hybrid TEM measurement. The Figure 8 discussion attributes broader hybrid PL tentatively to possible changes in CdS surface structure and particle size. These are distinct source-attributed interpretations, not resolved measurements. CdS suspension has approximate 425 and 600 nm bands with 325 nm excitation; the 1.5 wt% hybrid film has stronger, broader emission. No graph-only intensities, linewidths or quantum yields are extracted.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 4, Figures7–8 and optical discussion

intuition.title: Infrared prose and figure disagree
intuition.text: Hydroxyl-coated CdS prose gives 1105 and 1020 cm−1 (C–O),2926 and 2850 cm−1 (C–H), and 1440 cm−1 (CH2); Figure 6a labels 2960 rather than 2926 cm−1. TDI-modified CdS has 2262 cm−1 (NCO) and 1712 cm−1 (carbamate). The 2960/2926 discrepancy is preserved.

intuition.title: Four preparation conditions, one common colloid precursor
intuition.text: S1 is the hydrolyzed and acid-peptized reference colloid. S2 treats a 100 cm3 aliquot for 15 h at 200°C in a 200 cm3 Parr bomb, then cools for 2 h and stands for 24 h. S3 and S4 use 30 cm3 aliquots in a microwave vessel; Table 1 specifies 30 psi/10 min and 60 psi/5 min respectively. Independent physical batch identifiers are unknown.
intuition.source_locator: Main p.2, Experimental and Table 1

intuition.title: Temperature correlation is not a measured probe reading
intuition.text: The source correlates 30 psi to 121.5°C and 60 psi to 145°C using vaporization enthalpy tables. The 630 ± 50 W microwave is set at 80%, with a 2 min pressure ramp. Neither exact absorbed power nor a converted energy is inferred. The separate 544 W/12 min comparison remains attributed prose.
intuition.source_locator: Main pp.2 and 4

intuition.title: Table and figure labels disagree
intuition.text: Table 1 explicitly assigns S3 to 30 psi, correlated 121.5°C and TAP 10 min, and S4 to 60 psi, correlated 145°C and TAP 5 min. Figure 1 and Figure 7 plot keys instead print microwave 5 min at 30 PSI and 10 min at 60 PSI. Table-labeled canonical conditions are preserved alongside the contradictory plot keys; no guessed reconciliation. Figure 1 caption assigns a=S1 and b=S2, while its plot key labels a=hydrothermally treated and b=colloidal TiO2. Panel-specific sample identity is therefore unresolved; the caption and key remain separate. Figure 7 caption assigns a=S1, b=S4, c=S3, d=S2; its plot key instead labels a=microwave 5 min 30 PSI, b=microwave 10 min 60 PSI, c=colloidal TiO2, d=hydrothermally treated. No exact curve-to-recipe mapping is silently inferred.
intuition.source_locator: Main pp.2 and 4, Table 1 and Figures 1/7

intuition.title: Wet colloid and analytical specimens remain distinct
intuition.text: Each product is split equally; one half is dried at 80°C for 3 h for analysis. Raman and XRD explicitly use dried material. TEM uses ethanol-diluted samples on copper grids without expressly naming the wet/dried half. The whole colloid is not silently relabeled as dried powder.
intuition.source_locator: Main p.2, Experimental

intuition.title: Crystallite size differs from particle distribution
intuition.text: Table 2 Scherrer estimates for S1/S2/S3/S4 are 3.4/10.2/4.8/4.8 nm. TEM gives S1 3–35 nm, S2 approximately 10–15 nm and Figure 4 S3 approximately 5 nm with poor contrast. The broad S1 distribution and its source-interpreted 3–6 nm center are not interchangeable metrics.
intuition.source_locator: Main p.3, Table 2 and Figures 2–4

intuition.title: Electron diffraction carries an unresolved specimen label
intuition.text: Main p.4 prose identifies the microwave electron-diffraction specimen as S3, but Figure 6 caption identifies S4. Figure 6 is shared ambiguous microwave context and not evidence of a separately identified S3 or S4 physical batch. S2 Figure 5 reports less than 0.1% brookite with percentage basis unspecified. Brookite reference is PDF 29-1360 in p.2 prose but PDF 26-1360 in Figure 5 caption. Both printed designations remain visible; no corrected reference number or measured crystallographic file is supplied.
intuition.source_locator: Main pp.2–4, Figures 5–6

intuition.title: Raman supports a relative comparison
intuition.text: All 24 Table 3 cells are retained: relative peak heights with no printed units and normalized half-height widths printed in cm−1. The source associates narrower widths, symmetry and energy shifts with improved crystallinity. These are attributed interpretations, not measured crystallinity percentages. General bands at 514 and 639 cm−1 are assigned to A1g and Eg; the 200 to approximately 360 cm−1 region is assigned to brookite.
intuition.source_locator: Main pp.4–5, Figure 7 and Table 3

intuition.title: Applications are motivation, not measured devices
intuition.text: Electrochemical/photoelectrochemical efficiency is discussed as motivation and implication. This article provides no new fabricated device efficiency, measured atomic coordinates or refined unit cell. Literature temperatures and prior methods in the introduction are not additional recipes in this package.
intuition.source_locator: Main pp.1 and 5

intuition.title: Four preparation conditions, one common colloid precursor
intuition.text: S1 is the hydrolyzed and acid-peptized reference colloid. S2 treats a 100 cm3 aliquot for 15 h at 200°C in a 200 cm3 Parr bomb, then cools for 2 h and stands for 24 h. S3 and S4 use 30 cm3 aliquots in a microwave vessel; Table 1 specifies 30 psi/10 min and 60 psi/5 min respectively. Independent physical batch identifiers are unknown.
intuition.source_locator: Main p.2, Experimental and Table 1

intuition.title: Temperature correlation is not a measured probe reading
intuition.text: The source correlates 30 psi to 121.5°C and 60 psi to 145°C using vaporization enthalpy tables. The 630 ± 50 W microwave is set at 80%, with a 2 min pressure ramp. Neither exact absorbed power nor a converted energy is inferred. The separate 544 W/12 min comparison remains attributed prose.
intuition.source_locator: Main pp.2 and 4

intuition.title: Table and figure labels disagree
intuition.text: Table 1 explicitly assigns S3 to 30 psi, correlated 121.5°C and TAP 10 min, and S4 to 60 psi, correlated 145°C and TAP 5 min. Figure 1 and Figure 7 plot keys instead print microwave 5 min at 30 PSI and 10 min at 60 PSI. Table-labeled canonical conditions are preserved alongside the contradictory plot keys; no guessed reconciliation. Figure 1 caption assigns a=S1 and b=S2, while its plot key labels a=hydrothermally treated and b=colloidal TiO2. Panel-specific sample identity is therefore unresolved; the caption and key remain separate. Figure 7 caption assigns a=S1, b=S4, c=S3, d=S2; its plot key instead labels a=microwave 5 min 30 PSI, b=microwave 10 min 60 PSI, c=colloidal TiO2, d=hydrothermally treated. No exact curve-to-recipe mapping is silently inferred.
intuition.source_locator: Main pp.2 and 4, Table 1 and Figures 1/7

intuition.title: Wet colloid and analytical specimens remain distinct
intuition.text: Each product is split equally; one half is dried at 80°C for 3 h for analysis. Raman and XRD explicitly use dried material. TEM uses ethanol-diluted samples on copper grids without expressly naming the wet/dried half. The whole colloid is not silently relabeled as dried powder.
intuition.source_locator: Main p.2, Experimental

intuition.title: Crystallite size differs from particle distribution
intuition.text: Table 2 Scherrer estimates for S1/S2/S3/S4 are 3.4/10.2/4.8/4.8 nm. TEM gives S1 3–35 nm, S2 approximately 10–15 nm and Figure 4 S3 approximately 5 nm with poor contrast. The broad S1 distribution and its source-interpreted 3–6 nm center are not interchangeable metrics.
intuition.source_locator: Main p.3, Table 2 and Figures 2–4

intuition.title: Electron diffraction carries an unresolved specimen label
intuition.text: Main p.4 prose identifies the microwave electron-diffraction specimen as S3, but Figure 6 caption identifies S4. Figure 6 is shared ambiguous microwave context and not evidence of a separately identified S3 or S4 physical batch. S2 Figure 5 reports less than 0.1% brookite with percentage basis unspecified. Brookite reference is PDF 29-1360 in p.2 prose but PDF 26-1360 in Figure 5 caption. Both printed designations remain visible; no corrected reference number or measured crystallographic file is supplied.
intuition.source_locator: Main pp.2–4, Figures 5–6

intuition.title: Raman supports a relative comparison
intuition.text: All 24 Table 3 cells are retained: relative peak heights with no printed units and normalized half-height widths printed in cm−1. The source associates narrower widths, symmetry and energy shifts with improved crystallinity. These are attributed interpretations, not measured crystallinity percentages. General bands at 514 and 639 cm−1 are assigned to A1g and Eg; the 200 to approximately 360 cm−1 region is assigned to brookite.
intuition.source_locator: Main pp.4–5, Figure 7 and Table 3

intuition.title: Applications are motivation, not measured devices
intuition.text: Electrochemical/photoelectrochemical efficiency is discussed as motivation and implication. This article provides no new fabricated device efficiency, measured atomic coordinates or refined unit cell. Literature temperatures and prior methods in the introduction are not additional recipes in this package.

intuition.title: Four preparation conditions, one common colloid precursor
intuition.text: S1 is the hydrolyzed and acid-peptized reference colloid. S2 treats a 100 cm3 aliquot for 15 h at 200°C in a 200 cm3 Parr bomb, then cools for 2 h and stands for 24 h. S3 and S4 use 30 cm3 aliquots in a microwave vessel; Table 1 specifies 30 psi/10 min and 60 psi/5 min respectively. Independent physical batch identifiers are unknown.
intuition.source_locator: Main p.2, Experimental and Table 1

intuition.title: Temperature correlation is not a measured probe reading
intuition.text: The source correlates 30 psi to 121.5°C and 60 psi to 145°C using vaporization enthalpy tables. The 630 ± 50 W microwave is set at 80%, with a 2 min pressure ramp. Neither exact absorbed power nor a converted energy is inferred. The separate 544 W/12 min comparison remains attributed prose.
intuition.source_locator: Main pp.2 and 4

intuition.title: Table and figure labels disagree
intuition.text: Table 1 explicitly assigns S3 to 30 psi, correlated 121.5°C and TAP 10 min, and S4 to 60 psi, correlated 145°C and TAP 5 min. Figure 1 and Figure 7 plot keys instead print microwave 5 min at 30 PSI and 10 min at 60 PSI. Table-labeled canonical conditions are preserved alongside the contradictory plot keys; no guessed reconciliation. Figure 1 caption assigns a=S1 and b=S2, while its plot key labels a=hydrothermally treated and b=colloidal TiO2. Panel-specific sample identity is therefore unresolved; the caption and key remain separate. Figure 7 caption assigns a=S1, b=S4, c=S3, d=S2; its plot key instead labels a=microwave 5 min 30 PSI, b=microwave 10 min 60 PSI, c=colloidal TiO2, d=hydrothermally treated. No exact curve-to-recipe mapping is silently inferred.
intuition.source_locator: Main pp.2 and 4, Table 1 and Figures 1/7

intuition.title: Wet colloid and analytical specimens remain distinct
intuition.text: Each product is split equally; one half is dried at 80°C for 3 h for analysis. Raman and XRD explicitly use dried material. TEM uses ethanol-diluted samples on copper grids without expressly naming the wet/dried half. The whole colloid is not silently relabeled as dried powder.
intuition.source_locator: Main p.2, Experimental

intuition.title: Crystallite size differs from particle distribution
intuition.text: Table 2 Scherrer estimates for S1/S2/S3/S4 are 3.4/10.2/4.8/4.8 nm. TEM gives S1 3–35 nm, S2 approximately 10–15 nm and Figure 4 S3 approximately 5 nm with poor contrast. The broad S1 distribution and its source-interpreted 3–6 nm center are not interchangeable metrics.
intuition.source_locator: Main p.3, Table 2 and Figures 2–4

intuition.title: Electron diffraction carries an unresolved specimen label
intuition.text: Main p.4 prose identifies the microwave electron-diffraction specimen as S3, but Figure 6 caption identifies S4. Figure 6 is shared ambiguous microwave context and not evidence of a separately identified S3 or S4 physical batch. S2 Figure 5 reports less than 0.1% brookite with percentage basis unspecified. Brookite reference is PDF 29-1360 in p.2 prose but PDF 26-1360 in Figure 5 caption. Both printed designations remain visible; no corrected reference number or measured crystallographic file is supplied.
intuition.source_locator: Main pp.2–4, Figures 5–6

intuition.title: Raman supports a relative comparison
intuition.text: All 24 Table 3 cells are retained: relative peak heights with no printed units and normalized half-height widths printed in cm−1. The source associates narrower widths, symmetry and energy shifts with improved crystallinity. These are attributed interpretations, not measured crystallinity percentages. General bands at 514 and 639 cm−1 are assigned to A1g and Eg; the 200 to approximately 360 cm−1 region is assigned to brookite.
intuition.source_locator: Main pp.4–5, Figure 7 and Table 3

intuition.title: Applications are motivation, not measured devices
intuition.text: Electrochemical/photoelectrochemical efficiency is discussed as motivation and implication. This article provides no new fabricated device efficiency, measured atomic coordinates or refined unit cell. Literature temperatures and prior methods in the introduction are not additional recipes in this package.
intuition.source_locator: Main pp.1 and 5

intuition.title: Polymer end groups
intuition.text: Polymer 1 has H/Br ends. Coupling with organotin compound 2 gives cyano-end polymer 3; LiAlH4 reduction gives amino-end polymer 4. NMR and MALDI support end-group conversion; no atomistic polymer conformation is measured.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 1–5, Polymer preparations and Figures 1–2

intuition.title: Unresolved polymer quantities
intuition.text: The polymer 3 procedure prints 0.4 mg polymer 1 (~0.054 mmol), yet yields 0.37 g at 94%. Polymer 4 acidification prints 0.5 mL of 2 M HCl followed by 1 mL. The package retains these conflicts and does not repair either dose. Main p. 1, Scheme 1 labels toluene/DMF as 4:1, whereas SI pp. 2–3 specify 40 mL toluene and 8 mL DMF for polymer 3. This unresolved discrepancy is retained; neither stated charge is changed to enforce the scheme ratio.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 2–3, Polymer 3 and 4 preparation; Main PDF p. 1, Scheme 1

intuition.title: Nanorod growth and source sequence
intuition.text: The detailed SI loads CdO, TDPA and TOPO, heats until clear, adds TOP and injects selenium/TOP at 300 °C, then grows at 290 °C for 5 min. Main p. 1 instead summarizes CdO and Se solution injection. The detailed operational sequence is retained while both descriptions remain documented. About 7 nm diameter and 30 nm length are TEM estimates, not a unit cell or film-specific size.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 6, CdSe nanocrystals; Main PDF p. 1, CdSe preparation and dimensions

intuition.title: Pyridine exchange and blending
intuition.text: The whole rod batch is refluxed in pyridine for 24 h under argon. After workup, 15–20 mg/mL nanocrystal dispersion is mixed with 15.0 mg/mL polymer solution in pyridine/chloroform 1:9 v/v. Individual blend aliquots are unreported; the stock concentration range is not a value for every specimen.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 6, Cosolutions

intuition.title: TEM compositions remain distinct
intuition.text: SI thin films use 2000 rpm and 5 or 12 vol% CdSe; thicker films use 1000 rpm and 12, 26 or 43 vol%. Main Figure 1 separately labels 20 or 40 wt%. No weight-to-volume conversion or exact cross-document physical-sample identity is asserted. Source film thicknesses and spin times are unreported.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 7–8, TEM and Figures 3–4; Main PDF p. 2, Figure 1

intuition.title: Morphology and mechanism
intuition.text: The source describes more homogeneous dispersion and no visible aggregation with amino-end polymer 4, versus phase separation with polymer 1, in both thinner and thicker films. Amino coordination partially replacing pyridine and larger interfacial area are proposed explanations, not directly measured coordination or charge-separation rates.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Morphology and interpretation; SI PDF p. 7, TEM comparison

intuition.title: Photovoltaic interpretation
intuition.text: The source reports higher efficiency and current density for polymer 4, with similar fill factors. Favored CdSe ratios are approximately 40 vol% for polymer 4 and 65 vol% for polymer 1. These are source-interpreted optima, not newly reconstructed growth batches. UV–vis spectra of the two active films are described as essentially identical. No graph-only PCE, voltage, current or fill-factor points are digitized.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Device discussion and Figure 2; SI PDF p. 9–11, Performance and Figures 5–8

intuition.title: Instrument and label conflicts
intuition.text: General MALDI text gives 20 keV acceleration, whereas SI Figure 2 says 2000 V. SI Figure 6 caption repeats open-circuit voltage, while its axes/title and p. 9 identify current density. SI Figure 7 labels FF (%) with fractional-looking values. Original labels are retained; no correction or percent conversion is performed. SI p. 9 prints FF = max{J*V} / Jsc* Voc without denominator parentheses. The denominator grouping is unresolved in the printed typography; no fill factor is calculated. Figure 7 percent-axis ambiguity is retained.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 1, 5, 9–11, MALDI and device figure captions

intuition.title: Analytical details
intuition.text: Compound 2 elemental analysis: calculated C 35.33, H 4.08, N 5.15, S 11.79, Sn 43.65%; found C 35.30, H 4.12, N 5.16, S 11.78%; no found Sn value. Its 1H NMR in CDCl3: δ 7.70 (d, J 3.6 Hz, 1H), 7.16 (d, J 3.6 Hz, 1H), 0.43 (s, 9H). Polymer 3 has δ 7.58 and 7.11 (each d, J 3.9 Hz); polymer 4 has the end-group singlet at δ 4.10. These do not supply nanocrystal phase or coordinates.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 2–4, Elemental analysis, NMR and Figure 1

intuition.title: Morphology and mechanism

intuition.title: Instrument and label conflicts
intuition.text: General MALDI text gives 20 keV acceleration, whereas SI Figure 2 says 2000 V. SI Figure 6 caption repeats open-circuit voltage, while its axes/title and p. 9 identify current density. SI Figure 7 labels FF (%) with fractional-looking values. Original labels are retained; no correction or percent conversion is performed. SI p. 9 prints FF = max{J*V} / Jsc* Voc without denominator parentheses. The denominator grouping is unresolved in the printed typography; no fill factor is calculated. Figure 7 percent-axis ambiguity is retained.

intuition.title: Analytical details

Its 1H NMR in CDCl3: δ 7.70 (d, J 3.6 Hz, 1H), 7.16 (d, J 3.6 Hz, 1H), 0.43 (s, 9H). Polymer 3 has δ 7.58 and 7.11 (each d, J 3.9 Hz); polymer 4 has the end-group singlet at δ 4.10. These do not supply nanocrystal phase or coordinates.

intuition.text: The main article alone summarizes preparation; the locally identity-matched SI supplies polymer intermediates, CdSe growth, ligand exchange, TEM films, devices and measurement procedures. Its identity is checked, but it has no separate strict-screen PASS. Full cited works remain unreviewed.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 1–11, Complete SI

intuition.title: Polymer end groups
intuition.text: Polymer 1 has H/Br ends. Coupling with organotin compound 2 gives cyano-end polymer 3; LiAlH4 reduction gives amino-end polymer 4. NMR and MALDI support end-group conversion; no atomistic polymer conformation is measured.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 1–5, Polymer preparations and Figures 1–2

intuition.title: Unresolved polymer quantities
intuition.text: The polymer 3 procedure prints 0.4 mg polymer 1 (~0.054 mmol), yet yields 0.37 g at 94%. Polymer 4 acidification prints 0.5 mL of 2 M HCl followed by 1 mL. The package retains these conflicts and does not repair either dose. Main p. 1, Scheme 1 labels toluene/DMF as 4:1, whereas SI pp. 2–3 specify 40 mL toluene and 8 mL DMF for polymer 3. This unresolved discrepancy is retained; neither stated charge is changed to enforce the scheme ratio.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 2–3, Polymer 3 and 4 preparation; Main PDF p. 1, Scheme 1

intuition.title: Nanorod growth and source sequence
intuition.text: The detailed SI loads CdO, TDPA and TOPO, heats until clear, adds TOP and injects selenium/TOP at 300 °C, then grows at 290 °C for 5 min. Main p. 1 instead summarizes CdO and Se solution injection. The detailed operational sequence is retained while both descriptions remain documented. About 7 nm diameter and 30 nm length are TEM estimates, not a unit cell or film-specific size.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 6, CdSe nanocrystals; Main PDF p. 1, CdSe preparation and dimensions

intuition.title: Pyridine exchange and blending
intuition.text: The whole rod batch is refluxed in pyridine for 24 h under argon. After workup, 15–20 mg/mL nanocrystal dispersion is mixed with 15.0 mg/mL polymer solution in pyridine/chloroform 1:9 v/v. Individual blend aliquots are unreported; the stock concentration range is not a value for every specimen.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 6, Cosolutions

intuition.title: TEM compositions remain distinct
intuition.text: SI thin films use 2000 rpm and 5 or 12 vol% CdSe; thicker films use 1000 rpm and 12, 26 or 43 vol%. Main Figure 1 separately labels 20 or 40 wt%. No weight-to-volume conversion or exact cross-document physical-sample identity is asserted. Source film thicknesses and spin times are unreported.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 7–8, TEM and Figures 3–4; Main PDF p. 2, Figure 1

intuition.title: Morphology and mechanism
intuition.text: The source describes more homogeneous dispersion and no visible aggregation with amino-end polymer 4, versus phase separation with polymer 1, in both thinner and thicker films. Amino coordination partially replacing pyridine and larger interfacial area are proposed explanations, not directly measured coordination or charge-separation rates.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Morphology and interpretation; SI PDF p. 7, TEM comparison

intuition.title: Photovoltaic interpretation
intuition.text: The source reports higher efficiency and current density for polymer 4, with similar fill factors. Favored CdSe ratios are approximately 40 vol% for polymer 4 and 65 vol% for polymer 1. These are source-interpreted optima, not newly reconstructed growth batches. UV–vis spectra of the two active films are described as essentially identical. No graph-only PCE, voltage, current or fill-factor points are digitized.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Device discussion and Figure 2; SI PDF p. 9–11, Performance and Figures 5–8

intuition.title: Instrument and label conflicts
intuition.text: General MALDI text gives 20 keV acceleration, whereas SI Figure 2 says 2000 V. SI Figure 6 caption repeats open-circuit voltage, while its axes/title and p. 9 identify current density. SI Figure 7 labels FF (%) with fractional-looking values. Original labels are retained; no correction or percent conversion is performed. SI p. 9 prints FF = max{J*V} / Jsc* Voc without denominator parentheses. The denominator grouping is unresolved in the printed typography; no fill factor is calculated. Figure 7 percent-axis ambiguity is retained.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 1, 5, 9–11, MALDI and device figure captions

intuition.title: Analytical details
intuition.text: Compound 2 elemental analysis: calculated C 35.33, H 4.08, N 5.15, S 11.79, Sn 43.65%; found C 35.30, H 4.12, N 5.16, S 11.78%; no found Sn value. Its 1H NMR in CDCl3: δ 7.70 (d, J 3.6 Hz, 1H), 7.16 (d, J 3.6 Hz, 1H), 0.43 (s, 9H). Polymer 3 has δ 7.58 and 7.11 (each d, J 3.9 Hz); polymer 4 has the end-group singlet at δ 4.10. These do not supply nanocrystal phase or coordinates.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 2–4, Elemental analysis, NMR and Figure 1

Favored CdSe ratios are approximately 40 vol% for polymer 4 and 65 vol% for polymer 1. These are source-interpreted optima, not newly reconstructed growth batches. intuition.title: Instrument and label conflicts
intuition.text: General MALDI text gives 20 keV acceleration, whereas SI Figure 2 says 2000 V. SI Figure 6 caption repeats open-circuit voltage, while its axes/title and p. 9 identify current density. SI Figure 7 labels FF (%) with fractional-looking values. Original labels are retained; no correction or percent conversion is performed. SI p. 9 prints FF = max{J*V} / Jsc* Voc without denominator parentheses. The denominator grouping is unresolved in the printed typography; no fill factor is calculated. Figure 7 percent-axis ambiguity is retained.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 1, 5, 9–11, MALDI and device figure captions

intuition.title: Analytical details
intuition.text: Compound 2 elemental analysis: calculated C 35.33, H 4.08, N 5.15, S 11.79, Sn 43.65%; found C 35.30, H 4.12, N 5.16, S 11.78%; no found Sn value. Its 1H NMR in CDCl3: δ 7.70 (d, J 3.6 Hz, 1H), 7.16 (d, J 3.6 Hz, 1H), 0.43 (s, 9H). Polymer 3 has δ 7.58 and 7.11 (each d, J 3.9 Hz); polymer 4 has the end-group singlet at δ 4.10. These do not supply nanocrystal phase or coordinates.

intuition.title: Unresolved polymer quantities

intuition.title: Nanorod growth and source sequence
intuition.text: The detailed SI loads CdO, TDPA and TOPO, heats until clear, adds TOP and injects selenium/TOP at 300 °C, then grows at 290 °C for 5 min. Main p. 1 instead summarizes CdO and Se solution injection. The detailed operational sequence is retained while both descriptions remain documented. About 7 nm diameter and 30 nm length are TEM estimates, not a unit cell or film-specific size.

intuition.title: Pyridine exchange and blending
intuition.text: The whole rod batch is refluxed in pyridine for 24 h under argon. Individual blend aliquots are unreported; the stock concentration range is not a value for every specimen.

intuition.text: The polymer 3 procedure prints 0.4 mg polymer 1 (~0.054 mmol), yet yields 0.37 g at 94%. Polymer 4 acidification prints 0.5 mL of 2 M HCl followed by 1 mL. The package retains these conflicts and does not repair either dose. Main p. 1, Scheme 1 labels toluene/DMF as 4:1, whereas SI pp. 2–3 specify 40 mL toluene and 8 mL DMF for polymer 3. This unresolved discrepancy is retained; neither stated charge is changed to enforce the scheme ratio.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 2–3, Polymer 3 and 4 preparation; Main PDF p. 1, Scheme 1

intuition.title: Nanorod growth and source sequence
intuition.text: The detailed SI loads CdO, TDPA and TOPO, heats until clear, adds TOP and injects selenium/TOP at 300 °C, then grows at 290 °C for 5 min. Main p. 1 instead summarizes CdO and Se solution injection. The detailed operational sequence is retained while both descriptions remain documented. About 7 nm diameter and 30 nm length are TEM estimates, not a unit cell or film-specific size.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 6, CdSe nanocrystals; Main PDF p. 1, CdSe preparation and dimensions

intuition.title: Pyridine exchange and blending
intuition.text: The whole rod batch is refluxed in pyridine for 24 h under argon. After workup, 15–20 mg/mL nanocrystal dispersion is mixed with 15.0 mg/mL polymer solution in pyridine/chloroform 1:9 v/v. Individual blend aliquots are unreported; the stock concentration range is not a value for every specimen.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 6, Cosolutions

intuition.title: TEM compositions remain distinct
intuition.text: SI thin films use 2000 rpm and 5 or 12 vol% CdSe; thicker films use 1000 rpm and 12, 26 or 43 vol%. Main Figure 1 separately labels 20 or 40 wt%. intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 7–8, TEM and Figures 3–4; Main PDF p. 2, Figure 1

intuition.title: Morphology and mechanism
intuition.text: The source describes more homogeneous dispersion and no visible aggregation with amino-end polymer 4, versus phase separation with polymer 1, in both thinner and thicker films. Amino coordination partially replacing pyridine and larger interfacial area are proposed explanations, not directly measured coordination or charge-separation rates.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Morphology and interpretation; SI PDF p. 7, TEM comparison

intuition.title: Photovoltaic interpretation
intuition.text: The source reports higher efficiency and current density for polymer 4, with similar fill factors. Favored CdSe ratios are approximately 40 vol% for polymer 4 and 65 vol% for polymer 1. These are source-interpreted optima, not newly reconstructed growth batches. UV–vis spectra of the two active films are described as essentially identical. No graph-only PCE, voltage, current or fill-factor points are digitized.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Device discussion and Figure 2; SI PDF p. 9–11, Performance and Figures 5–8

intuition.title: Instrument and label conflicts
intuition.text: General MALDI text gives 20 keV acceleration, whereas SI Figure 2 says 2000 V. SI Figure 6 caption repeats open-circuit voltage, while its axes/title and p. 9 identify current density. SI Figure 7 labels FF (%) with fractional-looking values. Original labels are retained; no correction or percent conversion is performed. SI p. 9 prints FF = max{J*V} / Jsc* Voc without denominator parentheses. The denominator grouping is unresolved in the printed typography; no fill factor is calculated. Figure 7 percent-axis ambiguity is retained.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 1, 5, 9–11, MALDI and device figure captions

intuition.title: Analytical details
intuition.text: Compound 2 elemental analysis: calculated C 35.33, H 4.08, N 5.15, S 11.79, Sn 43.65%; found C 35.30, H 4.12, N 5.16, S 11.78%; no found Sn value. Its 1H NMR in CDCl3: δ 7.70 (d, J 3.6 Hz, 1H), 7.16 (d, J 3.6 Hz, 1H), 0.43 (s, 9H). Polymer 3 has δ 7.58 and 7.11 (each d, J 3.9 Hz); polymer 4 has the end-group singlet at δ 4.10. These do not supply nanocrystal phase or coordinates.

intuition.title: Polymer end groups
intuition.text: Polymer 1 has H/Br ends. Coupling with organotin compound 2 gives cyano-end polymer 3; LiAlH4 reduction gives amino-end polymer 4. NMR and MALDI support end-group conversion; no atomistic polymer conformation is measured.

intuition.title: Unresolved polymer quantities
intuition.text: The polymer 3 procedure prints 0.4 mg polymer 1 (~0.054 mmol), yet yields 0.37 g at 94%. Polymer 4 acidification prints 0.5 mL of 2 M HCl followed by 1 mL. The package retains these conflicts and does not repair either dose. Main p. 1, Scheme 1 labels toluene/DMF as 4:1, whereas SI pp. 2–3 specify 40 mL toluene and 8 mL DMF for polymer 3. This unresolved discrepancy is retained; neither stated charge is changed to enforce the scheme ratio.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 2–3, Polymer 3 and 4 preparation; Main PDF p. 1, Scheme 1

intuition.title: Nanorod growth and source sequence
intuition.text: The detailed SI loads CdO, TDPA and TOPO, heats until clear, adds TOP and injects selenium/TOP at 300 °C, then grows at 290 °C for 5 min. Main p. 1 instead summarizes CdO and Se solution injection. The detailed operational sequence is retained while both descriptions remain documented. About 7 nm diameter and 30 nm length are TEM estimates, not a unit cell or film-specific size.

intuition.title: Pyridine exchange and blending
intuition.text: The whole rod batch is refluxed in pyridine for 24 h under argon. Individual blend aliquots are unreported; the stock concentration range is not a value for every specimen.

intuition.title: TEM compositions remain distinct
intuition.text: SI thin films use 2000 rpm and 5 or 12 vol% CdSe; thicker films use 1000 rpm and 12, 26 or 43 vol%. Main Figure 1 separately labels 20 or 40 wt%. intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 7–8, TEM and Figures 3–4; Main PDF p. 2, Figure 1

intuition.title: Morphology and mechanism
intuition.text: The source describes more homogeneous dispersion and no visible aggregation with amino-end polymer 4, versus phase separation with polymer 1, in both thinner and thicker films. Amino coordination partially replacing pyridine and larger interfacial area are proposed explanations, not directly measured coordination or charge-separation rates.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Morphology and interpretation; SI PDF p. 7, TEM comparison

intuition.title: Photovoltaic interpretation
intuition.text: The source reports higher efficiency and current density for polymer 4, with similar fill factors. Favored CdSe ratios are approximately 40 vol% for polymer 4 and 65 vol% for polymer 1. These are source-interpreted optima, not newly reconstructed growth batches. UV–vis spectra of the two active films are described as essentially identical. No graph-only PCE, voltage, current or fill-factor points are digitized.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Device discussion and Figure 2; SI PDF p. 9–11, Performance and Figures 5–8

intuition.title: Instrument and label conflicts
intuition.text: General MALDI text gives 20 keV acceleration, whereas SI Figure 2 says 2000 V. SI Figure 6 caption repeats open-circuit voltage, while its axes/title and p. 9 identify current density. SI Figure 7 labels FF (%) with fractional-looking values. Original labels are retained; no correction or percent conversion is performed. SI p. 9 prints FF = max{J*V} / Jsc* Voc without denominator parentheses. The denominator grouping is unresolved in the printed typography; no fill factor is calculated. Figure 7 percent-axis ambiguity is retained.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 1, 5, 9–11, MALDI and device figure captions

intuition.title: Analytical details
intuition.text: Compound 2 elemental analysis: calculated C 35.33, H 4.08, N 5.15, S 11.79, Sn 43.65%; found C 35.30, H 4.12, N 5.16, S 11.78%; no found Sn value. Its 1H NMR in CDCl3: δ 7.70 (d, J 3.6 Hz, 1H), 7.16 (d, J 3.6 Hz, 1H), 0.43 (s, 9H). Polymer 3 has δ 7.58 and 7.11 (each d, J 3.9 Hz); polymer 4 has the end-group singlet at δ 4.10. These do not supply nanocrystal phase or coordinates.

intuition.title: Full source scope
intuition.text: The main article alone summarizes preparation; the locally identity-matched SI supplies polymer intermediates, CdSe growth, ligand exchange, TEM films, devices and measurement procedures. Its identity is checked, but it has no separate strict-screen PASS. Full cited works remain unreviewed.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 1–11, Complete SI

intuition.title: Polymer end groups
intuition.text: Polymer 1 has H/Br ends. Coupling with organotin compound 2 gives cyano-end polymer 3; LiAlH4 reduction gives amino-end polymer 4. NMR and MALDI support end-group conversion; no atomistic polymer conformation is measured.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 1–5, Polymer preparations and Figures 1–2

intuition.title: Unresolved polymer quantities
intuition.text: The polymer 3 procedure prints 0.4 mg polymer 1 (~0.054 mmol), yet yields 0.37 g at 94%. Polymer 4 acidification prints 0.5 mL of 2 M HCl followed by 1 mL. The package retains these conflicts and does not repair either dose. Main p. 1, Scheme 1 labels toluene/DMF as 4:1, whereas SI pp. 2–3 specify 40 mL toluene and 8 mL DMF for polymer 3. This unresolved discrepancy is retained; neither stated charge is changed to enforce the scheme ratio.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 2–3, Polymer 3 and 4 preparation; Main PDF p. 1, Scheme 1

intuition.title: Nanorod growth and source sequence
intuition.text: The detailed SI loads CdO, TDPA and TOPO, heats until clear, adds TOP and injects selenium/TOP at 300 °C, then grows at 290 °C for 5 min. Main p. 1 instead summarizes CdO and Se solution injection. The detailed operational sequence is retained while both descriptions remain documented. About 7 nm diameter and 30 nm length are TEM estimates, not a unit cell or film-specific size.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 6, CdSe nanocrystals; Main PDF p. 1, CdSe preparation and dimensions

intuition.title: Pyridine exchange and blending
intuition.text: The whole rod batch is refluxed in pyridine for 24 h under argon. After workup, 15–20 mg/mL nanocrystal dispersion is mixed with 15.0 mg/mL polymer solution in pyridine/chloroform 1:9 v/v. Individual blend aliquots are unreported; the stock concentration range is not a value for every specimen.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 6, Cosolutions

intuition.title: TEM compositions remain distinct
intuition.text: SI thin films use 2000 rpm and 5 or 12 vol% CdSe; thicker films use 1000 rpm and 12, 26 or 43 vol%. Main Figure 1 separately labels 20 or 40 wt%. No weight-to-volume conversion or exact cross-document physical-sample identity is asserted. Source film thicknesses and spin times are unreported.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 7–8, TEM and Figures 3–4; Main PDF p. 2, Figure 1

intuition.title: Morphology and mechanism
intuition.text: The source describes more homogeneous dispersion and no visible aggregation with amino-end polymer 4, versus phase separation with polymer 1, in both thinner and thicker films. Amino coordination partially replacing pyridine and larger interfacial area are proposed explanations, not directly measured coordination or charge-separation rates.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Morphology and interpretation; SI PDF p. 7, TEM comparison

intuition.title: Photovoltaic interpretation
intuition.text: The source reports higher efficiency and current density for polymer 4, with similar fill factors. Favored CdSe ratios are approximately 40 vol% for polymer 4 and 65 vol% for polymer 1. These are source-interpreted optima, not newly reconstructed growth batches. UV–vis spectra of the two active films are described as essentially identical. No graph-only PCE, voltage, current or fill-factor points are digitized.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Device discussion and Figure 2; SI PDF p. 9–11, Performance and Figures 5–8

intuition.title: Instrument and label conflicts
intuition.text: General MALDI text gives 20 keV acceleration, whereas SI Figure 2 says 2000 V. SI Figure 6 caption repeats open-circuit voltage, while its axes/title and p. 9 identify current density. SI Figure 7 labels FF (%) with fractional-looking values. Original labels are retained; no correction or percent conversion is performed. SI p. 9 prints FF = max{J*V} / Jsc* Voc without denominator parentheses. The denominator grouping is unresolved in the printed typography; no fill factor is calculated. Figure 7 percent-axis ambiguity is retained.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 1, 5, 9–11, MALDI and device figure captions

intuition.title: Analytical details
intuition.text: Compound 2 elemental analysis: calculated C 35.33, H 4.08, N 5.15, S 11.79, Sn 43.65%; found C 35.30, H 4.12, N 5.16, S 11.78%; no found Sn value. Its 1H NMR in CDCl3: δ 7.70 (d, J 3.6 Hz, 1H), 7.16 (d, J 3.6 Hz, 1H), 0.43 (s, 9H). Polymer 3 has δ 7.58 and 7.11 (each d, J 3.9 Hz); polymer 4 has the end-group singlet at δ 4.10. These do not supply nanocrystal phase or coordinates.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 2–4, Elemental analysis, NMR and Figure 1

intuition.title: Hydrothermal precursor and postannealed oxide
intuition.text: Hydrothermal processing first produces orthorhombic InOOH. Annealing at 500 °C for 1 h in normal atmosphere gives rhombohedral In2O3. Separate records preserve the intermediate and final phases with explicit parent-record lineage; these are stages of two vessel routes, not four unrelated physical batches.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Experimental synthesis; Figure 1 and second-vessel comparison

intuition.title: Two vessels with different reported detail
intuition.text: The first experiment uses a stirred 300 mL stainless-steel pressure vessel, 0.7 M aqueous indium nitrate monohydrate, 200 °C and 4 h. The second uses a 50 mL Teflon-lined autoclave without stirring. The source calls its filtration, washing and drying similar to the first case; its hydrothermal concentration, temperature and dwell are not independently restated. Vessel capacities do not establish liquid charges.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1, Experimental synthesis paragraph

intuition.title: Reference cells are not specimen refinements
intuition.text: For orthorhombic InOOH, cited reference values are a = 5.260 Å, b = 4.560 Å and c = 3.270 Å; the first hydrothermal specimen refines to 5.262, 4.591 and 3.258 Å. For rhombohedral In2O3, reference a = 5.487 Å and c = 14.510 Å differ from the first annealed specimen values 5.469 and 14.491 Å. Only the refined specimen values enter product measurements. No atomic coordinates are supplied.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1, XRD phase indexing and lattice refinements

intuition.title: XRD sizes and TEM have distinct evidence
intuition.text: The annealed stainless-steel route has a Scherrer mean of 12 nm and reported range 10–18 nm. The continuing XRD comparison gives a mean of 22 nm and range 19–26 nm for the annealed Teflon-lined route. These are author-reported size estimates, not newly counted TEM distributions. Figure 2a qualitatively confirms nanometer particles only for the stainless-steel route; its 100 nm scale bar is not a particle diameter.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Scherrer estimate, second-vessel comparison and Figure 2

intuition.title: Stirring is an interpretation, not an isolated causal test
intuition.text: The authors attribute the size difference to stirring effects. The experiments also use different vessel capacities and liner materials, and not every second-experiment condition is restated. The attribution is retained as the authors’ interpretation without treating it as a controlled one-variable law.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Particle-dimension comparison

intuition.title: Phase evidence and application motivation
intuition.text: Figure 1b indexes rhombohedral In2O3, R-3c (167), ASTM 22-336. The authors report no detectable XRD peaks from other indium compounds; this does not establish an absolute chemical-purity limit. Figure 2b supports rhombohedral diffraction for the first annealed specimen. Introductory conductivity and sensing claims refer to background literature, not measurements on these powders.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Introduction, phase analysis and TEM/SAED discussion

intuition.title: Two vessels with different reported detail

intuition.title: Reference cells are not specimen refinements
intuition.text: For orthorhombic InOOH, cited reference values are a = 5.260 Å, b = 4.560 Å and c = 3.270 Å; the first hydrothermal specimen refines to 5.262, 4.591 and 3.258 Å. nominalTarget.label: Intended product composition
nominalTarget.scope: Intended and observed products are distinct for ratio comparisons.

intuition.title: A quantified solvothermal preparation
intuition.text: The main route uses 7 mmol CuCl2·2H2O and 4 mmol Te in ethylenediamine. The solvent fills 85% of a 100 mL Teflon-lined autoclave before the two solids are added successively. A sealed 160 °C treatment for 10 h, natural cooling, filtration, water/ethanol washing and vacuum drying at 60 °C for 4 h produce the specimen characterized in Figures 1–3.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Experimental procedure

intuition.title: Phase, crystallite size and particle diameter
intuition.text: Figure 1 indexes hexagonal Cu7Te4 with a = 8.335 Å and c = 7.211 Å, close to JCPDS 18-456. The source estimates a crystallite size of about 15 nm by the Scherrer formula. Figure 3 separately shows homogeneous nanoparticles with an average TEM diameter near 15 nm. These two approximate estimates use different methods and do not establish a measured coordinate model or a particle-size distribution.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Figures 1 and 3 and accompanying analysis

intuition.title: XPS composition and a printed unit anomaly
intuition.text: The reported Cu 2p and Te 3d peak positions are 932.4 eV and 572.7 eV. Peak quantification gives Cu:Te = 63.41:36.29; this ratio is retained without renormalization. The printed charge reference is C 1s at 284.60 kV, although specimen peaks and plotted axes use eV. That unit anomaly remains unresolved. The source reports no obvious oxide peaks but provides no impurity detection limit.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Figure 2 and XPS discussion

intuition.title: Solvent comparisons and author-proposed mechanism
intuition.text: Benzene and diethylamine comparisons did not react tellurium with copper chloride. The authors propose that polar, bidentate ethylenediamine stabilizes metal-polytellurido intermediates and promotes dissolution, diffusion and crystallization while absorbing reaction heat. They compare quoted solvent critical temperatures of 318 °C for ethylenediamine and 374 °C for water. These are explanatory source context, not measured synthesis temperatures or identified intermediates.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Solvent and reaction-mechanism discussion

intuition.title: Feed-ratio and precursor comparisons
intuition.text: A 3:2 copper-salt/Te feed gives Cu7Te4 mixed with unreacted tellurium rather than the expected Cu3Te2. A 2:1 feed gives only hexagonal Cu7Te4 rather than Cu2Te. Replacing CuCl2 with CuI also gives Cu7Te4 nanoparticles. The source does not separately assign absolute charges, complete conditions, particle sizes or displayed figures to these comparisons; they remain supporting contexts.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Molar-ratio and CuI substitution paragraph

intuition.title: An unresolved intermediate and further heating
intuition.text: At 140 °C an XRD-observed intermediate could not be identified against the available JCPDS patterns. Its assignment as a Cu/Te/ethylenediamine complex is the authors’ inference. Further heating of this intermediate at 180 °C produces Cu7Te4 described as pure, with no treatment time or numerical purity limit supplied. Below 120 °C, neither the intermediate nor reacted tellurium is reported. The 180 °C context retains explicit lineage from the 140 °C intermediate without inventing its formula or handling.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Temperature-dependent intermediate discussion

intuition.title: Application motivation is not a measured property
intuition.text: The introduction discusses thermoelectric applications, thermopower, electrical resistivity and thermal conductivity using cited literature. No numerical thermoelectric property is measured on these Cu7Te4 powders. Cited full papers remain unreviewed and do not supply missing experimental conditions.

intuition.title: A quantified solvothermal preparation
intuition.text: The main route uses 7 mmol CuCl2·2H2O and 4 mmol Te in ethylenediamine. The solvent fills 85% of a 100 mL Teflon-lined autoclave before the two solids are added successively. A sealed 160 °C treatment for 10 h, natural cooling, filtration, water/ethanol washing and vacuum drying at 60 °C for 4 h produce the specimen characterized in Figures 1–3.
