intuition.title: Phase, crystallite size and particle diameter
intuition.text: Figure 1 indexes hexagonal Cu7Te4 with a = 8.335 Å and c = 7.211 Å, close to JCPDS 18-456. The source estimates a crystallite size of about 15 nm by the Scherrer formula. Figure 3 separately shows homogeneous nanoparticles with an average TEM diameter near 15 nm. These two approximate estimates use different methods and do not establish a measured coordinate model or a particle-size distribution.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Figures 1 and 3 and accompanying analysis

intuition.title: XPS composition and a printed unit anomaly
intuition.text: The reported Cu 2p and Te 3d peak positions are 932.4 eV and 572.7 eV. Peak quantification gives Cu:Te = 63.41:36.29; this ratio is retained without renormalization. The printed charge reference is C 1s at 284.60 kV, although specimen peaks and plotted axes use eV. That unit anomaly remains unresolved. The source reports no obvious oxide peaks but provides no impurity detection limit.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Figure 2 and XPS discussion

intuition.title: Solvent comparisons and author-proposed mechanism
intuition.text: Benzene and diethylamine comparisons did not react tellurium with copper chloride. The authors propose that polar, bidentate ethylenediamine stabilizes metal-polytellurido intermediates and promotes dissolution, diffusion and crystallization while absorbing reaction heat. They compare quoted solvent critical temperatures of 318 °C for ethylenediamine and 374 °C for water. These are explanatory source context, not measured synthesis temperatures or identified intermediates.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Solvent and reaction-mechanism discussion

intuition.title: Feed-ratio and precursor comparisons
intuition.text: A 3:2 copper-salt/Te feed gives Cu7Te4 mixed with unreacted tellurium rather than the expected Cu3Te2. A 2:1 feed gives only hexagonal Cu7Te4 rather than Cu2Te. Replacing CuCl2 with CuI also gives Cu7Te4 nanoparticles. The source does not separately assign absolute charges, complete conditions, particle sizes or displayed figures to these comparisons; they remain supporting contexts.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Molar-ratio and CuI substitution paragraph

intuition.title: An unresolved intermediate and further heating
intuition.text: At 140 °C an XRD-observed intermediate could not be identified against the available JCPDS patterns. Its assignment as a Cu/Te/ethylenediamine complex is the authors’ inference. Further heating of this intermediate at 180 °C produces Cu7Te4 described as pure, with no treatment time or numerical purity limit supplied. Below 120 °C, neither the intermediate nor reacted tellurium is reported. The 180 °C context retains explicit lineage from the 140 °C intermediate without inventing its formula or handling.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Temperature-dependent intermediate discussion

The printed charge reference is C 1s at 284.60 kV, although specimen peaks and plotted axes use eV. That unit anomaly remains unresolved. The source reports no obvious oxide peaks but provides no impurity detection limit.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Figure 2 and XPS discussion

intuition.title: Solvent comparisons and author-proposed mechanism
intuition.text: Benzene and diethylamine comparisons did not react tellurium with copper chloride. The authors propose that polar, bidentate ethylenediamine stabilizes metal-polytellurido intermediates and promotes dissolution, diffusion and crystallization while absorbing reaction heat. They compare quoted solvent critical temperatures of 318 °C for ethylenediamine and 374 °C for water. These are explanatory source context, not measured synthesis temperatures or identified intermediates.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Solvent and reaction-mechanism discussion

intuition.title: Feed-ratio and precursor comparisons
intuition.text: A 3:2 copper-salt/Te feed gives Cu7Te4 mixed with unreacted tellurium rather than the expected Cu3Te2. A 2:1 feed gives only hexagonal Cu7Te4 rather than Cu2Te. Replacing CuCl2 with CuI also gives Cu7Te4 nanoparticles. The source does not separately assign absolute charges, complete conditions, particle sizes or displayed figures to these comparisons; they remain supporting contexts.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Molar-ratio and CuI substitution paragraph

intuition.title: An unresolved intermediate and further heating
intuition.text: At 140 °C an XRD-observed intermediate could not be identified against the available JCPDS patterns. Its assignment as a Cu/Te/ethylenediamine complex is the authors’ inference. Further heating of this intermediate at 180 °C produces Cu7Te4 described as pure, with no treatment time or numerical purity limit supplied. Below 120 °C, neither the intermediate nor reacted tellurium is reported. The 180 °C context retains explicit lineage from the 140 °C intermediate without inventing its formula or handling.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Temperature-dependent intermediate discussion

intuition.title: Application motivation is not a measured property
intuition.text: The introduction discusses thermoelectric applications, thermopower, electrical resistivity and thermal conductivity using cited literature. No numerical thermoelectric property is measured on these Cu7Te4 powders. Cited full papers remain unreviewed and do not supply missing experimental conditions.

intuition.title: Powder and film use different charges
intuition.text: The powder recipe uses 0.10 g TiF4 and 160 °C for 24 h. The coloured film uses 0.010 g TiF4, adds 5 mL tert-butyl alcohol and reacts at 130 °C for 24 h with titanium foil present. Vessel capacity is 50 mL in both protocols, not a reported liquid volume.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 1, Sample preparation

intuition.title: Early precursor, sheets and stacks are different objects
intuition.text: The 3 h material is an amorphous organic-rich titanium precursor. Later crystallinity, lamellar spacing, plate thickness and overall assembly dimensions describe different structural levels. The source supplies fixed temperature and stoichiometry for the time series, but does not separately restate each absolute charge.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Figure 2 time series; SI PDF p. 3, Figure S3

intuition.title: Stoichiometry changes assembly
intuition.text: Ratios TiF4:benzyl alcohol = 1:4800, 1:1200, 1:600 and 1:240 are separate comparisons at 160 °C for 24 h. A useful range 1:2400 to 1:300 is stated in the discussion, not a list of individually measured specimens. High fluoride loading is proposed to generate excess HF that etches (001) facets; neither HF concentration nor this mechanism is directly measured.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Ratio discussion; SI PDF p. 2, Figure S2

intuition.title: Surface-mediated assembly is an author model
intuition.text: Figure 3 proposes benzyl groups and π stacking between sheets. The text gives adjacent surface Ti separation about 0.4 nm and model interlayer spacing 0.92 nm; the diagram also labels 0.38 and 0.76 nm along the surface. These are model dimensions, distinct from the approximately 1.3 nm HRTEM spacing in the 5 h specimen. No source coordinates or unit-cell model are supplied.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Figure 3 and model discussion

intuition.title: Alcohol identity affects stacking
intuition.text: Pentafluorobenzyl alcohol alone gives no sheets or stacking. Its 1:1 v/v mixture with benzyl alcohol restores organized stacks with a reported gap of 5 ± 2 nm. Among the para-halogen examples, fluoro gives stacked sheets while chloro and bromo give sheets without stacking. Substituent size and aromatic interactions are the authors’ explanations, not measured molecular structures. Aliphatic-alcohol negative observations retain their missing separate conditions.

intuition.title: Early precursor, sheets and stacks are different objects
intuition.text: The 3 h material is an amorphous organic-rich titanium precursor. The source supplies fixed temperature and stoichiometry for the time series, but does not separately restate each absolute charge.

intuition.title: Stoichiometry changes assembly
intuition.text: Ratios TiF4:benzyl alcohol = 1:4800, 1:1200, 1:600 and 1:240 are separate comparisons at 160 °C for 24 h. A useful range 1:2400 to 1:300 is stated in the discussion, not a list of individually measured specimens. High fluoride loading is proposed to generate excess HF that etches (001) facets; neither HF concentration nor this mechanism is directly measured.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Ratio discussion; SI PDF p. 2, Figure S2

intuition.title: Surface-mediated assembly is an author model
intuition.text: Figure 3 proposes benzyl groups and π stacking between sheets. The text gives adjacent surface Ti separation about 0.4 nm and model interlayer spacing 0.92 nm; the diagram also labels 0.38 and 0.76 nm along the surface. These are model dimensions, distinct from the approximately 1.3 nm HRTEM spacing in the 5 h specimen. No source coordinates or unit-cell model are supplied.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Figure 3 and model discussion

intuition.title: Alcohol identity affects stacking
intuition.text: Pentafluorobenzyl alcohol alone gives no sheets or stacking. Its 1:1 v/v mixture with benzyl alcohol restores organized stacks with a reported gap of 5 ± 2 nm. Among the para-halogen examples, fluoro gives stacked sheets while chloro and bromo give sheets without stacking. Substituent size and aromatic interactions are the authors’ explanations, not measured molecular structures. Aliphatic-alcohol negative observations retain their missing separate conditions.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Alcohol discussion; SI PDF p. 4–5, Figures S5–S6

intuition.title: Organic content and FTIR comparisons
intuition.text: Figure S3 reports losses of 78, 64, 43, 38, 33 and 24% at reaction times 3, 5, 8, 12, 18 and 24 h, respectively. Its printed axis convention is retained. The authors assign 1489 cm−1 to aromatic rings and broad features at 3010 and 2893 cm−1 to interactions at the TiO2 surface. The latter features are absent for physisorbed benzyl alcohol on commercial P25. Figure S4 includes 12 h and 24 h products, pure P25, adsorbed P25 and pure benzyl alcohol. Adsorption preparation is unreported.

intuition.title: Powder and film use different charges
intuition.text: The powder recipe uses 0.10 g TiF4 and 160 °C for 24 h. The coloured film uses 0.010 g TiF4, adds 5 mL tert-butyl alcohol and reacts at 130 °C for 24 h with titanium foil present. Vessel capacity is 50 mL in both protocols, not a reported liquid volume.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 1, Sample preparation

intuition.title: Early precursor, sheets and stacks are different objects
intuition.text: The 3 h material is an amorphous organic-rich titanium precursor. Later crystallinity, lamellar spacing, plate thickness and overall assembly dimensions describe different structural levels. The source supplies fixed temperature and stoichiometry for the time series, but does not separately restate each absolute charge.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Figure 2 time series; SI PDF p. 3, Figure S3

intuition.title: Stoichiometry changes assembly
intuition.text: Ratios TiF4:benzyl alcohol = 1:4800, 1:1200, 1:600 and 1:240 are separate comparisons at 160 °C for 24 h. A useful range 1:2400 to 1:300 is stated in the discussion, not a list of individually measured specimens. High fluoride loading is proposed to generate excess HF that etches (001) facets; neither HF concentration nor this mechanism is directly measured.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Ratio discussion; SI PDF p. 2, Figure S2

intuition.title: Surface-mediated assembly is an author model
intuition.text: Figure 3 proposes benzyl groups and π stacking between sheets. The text gives adjacent surface Ti separation about 0.4 nm and model interlayer spacing 0.92 nm; the diagram also labels 0.38 and 0.76 nm along the surface. These are model dimensions, distinct from the approximately 1.3 nm HRTEM spacing in the 5 h specimen. No source coordinates or unit-cell model are supplied.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Figure 3 and model discussion

intuition.title: Alcohol identity affects stacking
intuition.text: Pentafluorobenzyl alcohol alone gives no sheets or stacking. Its 1:1 v/v mixture with benzyl alcohol restores organized stacks with a reported gap of 5 ± 2 nm. Among the para-halogen examples, fluoro gives stacked sheets while chloro and bromo give sheets without stacking. Substituent size and aromatic interactions are the authors’ explanations, not measured molecular structures. Aliphatic-alcohol negative observations retain their missing separate conditions.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Alcohol discussion; SI PDF p. 4–5, Figures S5–S6

intuition.title: Organic content and FTIR comparisons
intuition.text: Figure S3 reports losses of 78, 64, 43, 38, 33 and 24% at reaction times 3, 5, 8, 12, 18 and 24 h, respectively. Its printed axis convention is retained. The authors assign 1489 cm−1 to aromatic rings and broad features at 3010 and 2893 cm−1 to interactions at the TiO2 surface. The latter features are absent for physisorbed benzyl alcohol on commercial P25. Figure S4 includes 12 h and 24 h products, pure P25, adsorbed P25 and pure benzyl alcohol. Adsorption preparation is unreported.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, TGA and FTIR discussion; SI PDF p. 3–4, Figures S3–S4

intuition.title: Colour and substrate scope
intuition.text: The green layered film on Ti foil is 190 ± 10 nm thick and has diffuse-reflectance bands near 400 and 640 nm. Conditions for every observed colour are not supplied. The sol-gel procedure explicitly coats glass, whereas its heading, main comparison and Figure S8 refer to Ti foil. The relationship is unresolved; comparison thickness is not silently assigned to the glass specimen.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Figure 4 and sol-gel comparison; SI PDF p. 1, 6, Sol-gel preparation and Figure S8

intuition.title: Background and incomplete alternatives
intuition.text: Introductory photovoltaic, photocatalytic and reflective-coating applications are motivation or prospective uses, not performance measurements of these samples. Reference note 15 says titanium alkoxides behave similarly when HF is added, but gives no complete additional recipe. Cited full sources are unreviewed.

intuition.title: Early precursor, sheets and stacks are different objects
intuition.text: The 3 h material is an amorphous organic-rich titanium precursor. Later crystallinity, lamellar spacing, plate thickness and overall assembly dimensions describe different structural levels. The source supplies fixed temperature and stoichiometry for the time series, but does not separately restate each absolute charge.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Figure 2 time series; SI PDF p. 3, Figure S3

intuition.title: Stoichiometry changes assembly
intuition.text: Ratios TiF4:benzyl alcohol = 1:4800, 1:1200, 1:600 and 1:240 are separate comparisons at 160 °C for 24 h. A useful range 1:2400 to 1:300 is stated in the discussion, not a list of individually measured specimens. High fluoride loading is proposed to generate excess HF that etches (001) facets; neither HF concentration nor this mechanism is directly measured.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Ratio discussion; SI PDF p. 2, Figure S2

intuition.title: Surface-mediated assembly is an author model
intuition.text: Figure 3 proposes benzyl groups and π stacking between sheets. The text gives adjacent surface Ti separation about 0.4 nm and model interlayer spacing 0.92 nm; the diagram also labels 0.38 and 0.76 nm along the surface. These are model dimensions, distinct from the approximately 1.3 nm HRTEM spacing in the 5 h specimen. No source coordinates or unit-cell model are supplied.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Figure 3 and model discussion

intuition.title: Alcohol identity affects stacking
intuition.text: Pentafluorobenzyl alcohol alone gives no sheets or stacking. Its 1:1 v/v mixture with benzyl alcohol restores organized stacks with a reported gap of 5 ± 2 nm. Among the para-halogen examples, fluoro gives stacked sheets while chloro and bromo give sheets without stacking. Substituent size and aromatic interactions are the authors’ explanations, not measured molecular structures. Aliphatic-alcohol negative observations retain their missing separate conditions.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Alcohol discussion; SI PDF p. 4–5, Figures S5–S6

intuition.title: Organic content and FTIR comparisons
intuition.text: Figure S3 reports losses of 78, 64, 43, 38, 33 and 24% at reaction times 3, 5, 8, 12, 18 and 24 h, respectively. Its printed axis convention is retained. The authors assign 1489 cm−1 to aromatic rings and broad features at 3010 and 2893 cm−1 to interactions at the TiO2 surface. The latter features are absent for physisorbed benzyl alcohol on commercial P25. Figure S4 includes 12 h and 24 h products, pure P25, adsorbed P25 and pure benzyl alcohol. Adsorption preparation is unreported.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, TGA and FTIR discussion; SI PDF p. 3–4, Figures S3–S4

intuition.title: Colour and substrate scope
intuition.text: The green layered film on Ti foil is 190 ± 10 nm thick and has diffuse-reflectance bands near 400 and 640 nm. Conditions for every observed colour are not supplied. The relationship is unresolved; comparison thickness is not silently assigned to the glass specimen.

intuition.title: Powder and film use different charges
intuition.text: The powder recipe uses 0.10 g TiF4 and 160 °C for 24 h. The coloured film uses 0.010 g TiF4, adds 5 mL tert-butyl alcohol and reacts at 130 °C for 24 h with titanium foil present. Vessel capacity is 50 mL in both protocols, not a reported liquid volume.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 1, Sample preparation

intuition.title: Early precursor, sheets and stacks are different objects
intuition.text: The 3 h material is an amorphous organic-rich titanium precursor. Later crystallinity, lamellar spacing, plate thickness and overall assembly dimensions describe different structural levels. The source supplies fixed temperature and stoichiometry for the time series, but does not separately restate each absolute charge.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Figure 2 time series; SI PDF p. 3, Figure S3

intuition.title: Stoichiometry changes assembly
intuition.text: Ratios TiF4:benzyl alcohol = 1:4800, 1:1200, 1:600 and 1:240 are separate comparisons at 160 °C for 24 h. A useful range 1:2400 to 1:300 is stated in the discussion, not a list of individually measured specimens. High fluoride loading is proposed to generate excess HF that etches (001) facets; neither HF concentration nor this mechanism is directly measured.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Ratio discussion; SI PDF p. 2, Figure S2

intuition.title: Surface-mediated assembly is an author model
intuition.text: Figure 3 proposes benzyl groups and π stacking between sheets. The text gives adjacent surface Ti separation about 0.4 nm and model interlayer spacing 0.92 nm; the diagram also labels 0.38 and 0.76 nm along the surface. These are model dimensions, distinct from the approximately 1.3 nm HRTEM spacing in the 5 h specimen. No source coordinates or unit-cell model are supplied.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Figure 3 and model discussion

intuition.title: Alcohol identity affects stacking
intuition.text: Pentafluorobenzyl alcohol alone gives no sheets or stacking. Its 1:1 v/v mixture with benzyl alcohol restores organized stacks with a reported gap of 5 ± 2 nm. Among the para-halogen examples, fluoro gives stacked sheets while chloro and bromo give sheets without stacking. Substituent size and aromatic interactions are the authors’ explanations, not measured molecular structures. Aliphatic-alcohol negative observations retain their missing separate conditions.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Alcohol discussion; SI PDF p. 4–5, Figures S5–S6

intuition.title: Organic content and FTIR comparisons
intuition.text: Figure S3 reports losses of 78, 64, 43, 38, 33 and 24% at reaction times 3, 5, 8, 12, 18 and 24 h, respectively. Its printed axis convention is retained. The authors assign 1489 cm−1 to aromatic rings and broad features at 3010 and 2893 cm−1 to interactions at the TiO2 surface. The latter features are absent for physisorbed benzyl alcohol on commercial P25. Figure S4 includes 12 h and 24 h products, pure P25, adsorbed P25 and pure benzyl alcohol. Adsorption preparation is unreported.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, TGA and FTIR discussion; SI PDF p. 3–4, Figures S3–S4

intuition.title: Colour and substrate scope
intuition.text: The green layered film on Ti foil is 190 ± 10 nm thick and has diffuse-reflectance bands near 400 and 640 nm. Conditions for every observed colour are not supplied. The sol-gel procedure explicitly coats glass, whereas its heading, main comparison and Figure S8 refer to Ti foil. The relationship is unresolved; comparison thickness is not silently assigned to the glass specimen.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Figure 4 and sol-gel comparison; SI PDF p. 1, 6, Sol-gel preparation and Figure S8

intuition.title: Background and incomplete alternatives
intuition.text: Introductory photovoltaic, photocatalytic and reflective-coating applications are motivation or prospective uses, not performance measurements of these samples. Reference note 15 says titanium alkoxides behave similarly when HF is added, but gives no complete additional recipe. Cited full sources are unreviewed.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1, 3, Introduction, conclusion and reference note 15

intuition.title: Three charges create three named composites
intuition.text: SnCl2·2H2O charges of 300, 600 and 1200 mg are paired with the same 100 mL aqueous GO input at 0.2 g/L. The products are SnO2/G-0.3, -0.6 and -1.2, respectively. All are stirred for 24 h at room temperature, collected, washed and dried at 100 °C. The GO preparation is cited rather than reproduced; this recipe starts from the supplied GO dispersion.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1, Section 2.1

intuition.title: Coupled redox is the authors’ interpretation
intuition.text: The authors interpret the process as Sn2+ oxidation coupled to GO deoxygenation, supported by SnO2 diffraction and changes in FTIR/XPS. The proposed transformation is not a balanced experimentally measured reaction equation. No unique oxygen content of GO or graphene, tin conversion yield or dissolved speciation is supplied.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–3, Preparation and structural/spectroscopic discussion

intuition.title: Size and structure describe different quantities
intuition.text: XRD gives tetragonal SnO2 and Scherrer domain sizes of 8.4, 7.8 and 8.4 nm for the three composites. The text’s less-than-10 nm TEM statement is scoped to SnO2/G-0.3. Figure 3 annotates d(110) = 0.34 nm in each sample panel. The predicted Bragg value 0.337 nm is reference interpretation, not a second measured lattice spacing. No unit-cell refinement or coordinates are supplied.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Figures 1–3 and results

intuition.title: More tin changes loading and morphology
intuition.text: TGA gives approximate SnO2 mass percentages of 63, 68 and 74%. The source attributes the slower increase in SnO2 fraction than tin charge to partial SnCl2 loss, without measuring a recovery balance. TEM indicates more oxide particles on smaller graphene sheets as tin charge increases; numerical sheet dimensions are unreported.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Morphology and TGA discussion

intuition.title: Spectral comparisons retain their scope
intuition.text: GO bands are assigned at 1401, 1735, 1220, 1052, 827 and 1620 cm−1. The source assigns the composite-series 606 cm−1 band to Sn–O and interprets loss of several oxygen-group bands as reduction. GO Raman G and D positions are 1591.3 and 1365.6 cm−1; composite D/G ratios are 1.13, 1.25 and 1.34. These ratios are not particle sizes. XPS binding energies are scoped to GO or the SnO2/G-0.3 comparison as stated.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, FTIR, Raman and XPS discussion

intuition.title: Electrode processing is a separate supporting route
intuition.text: Each composite is mixed with carbon black and PVDF at 80:15:5 by weight in NMP, doctor-bladed onto copper and vacuum-dried at 120 °C for 8 h. Cells use lithium foil, polypropylene separator and 1 M LiPF6 in EC/DMC (1:1 by weight), with overnight soaking. These steps support the electrochemical measurements and do not demonstrate new nanoparticle structures.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Section 2.3

intuition.title: Battery results are specimen-linked
intuition.text: At 200 mA/g between 0.01 and 1.5 V versus Li, reported reversible capacities are 541.3, 402.7 and 222.4 mAh/g. After 35 cycles, retentions are about 69.7, 34.2 and 33.6%; only the 0.3 specimen has a separately stated 35-cycle capacity, 377.3 mAh/g. The authors propose that larger graphene sheets and lower oxide coverage reduce pulverization and improve conduction. These mechanisms are interpretations, not directly measured stress or conductivity.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 4, Figure 7 and discussion

intuition.title: References and introductory values are not new product data
intuition.text: The introductory 782 mAh/g theoretical SnO2 capacity, literature bare-SnO2 performance and prospective sensor uses are background. No standalone pure SnO2 comparator synthesis is given here. All 33 bibliography entries are retained, but their full sources are unreviewed.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1, 4–5, Introduction, conclusion and bibliography

intuition.title: Three charges create three named composites
intuition.text: SnCl2·2H2O charges of 300, 600 and 1200 mg are paired with the same 100 mL aqueous GO input at 0.2 g/L. The products are SnO2/G-0.3, -0.6 and -1.2, respectively. All are stirred for 24 h at room temperature, collected, washed and dried at 100 °C. The GO preparation is cited rather than reproduced; this recipe starts from the supplied GO dispersion.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1, Section 2.1

intuition.title: Coupled redox is the authors’ interpretation
intuition.text: The authors interpret the process as Sn2+ oxidation coupled to GO deoxygenation, supported by SnO2 diffraction and changes in FTIR/XPS. The proposed transformation is not a balanced experimentally measured reaction equation. No unique oxygen content of GO or graphene, tin conversion yield or dissolved speciation is supplied.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–3, Preparation and structural/spectroscopic discussion

intuition.title: Size and structure describe different quantities
intuition.text: XRD gives tetragonal SnO2 and Scherrer domain sizes of 8.4, 7.8 and 8.4 nm for the three composites. The text’s less-than-10 nm TEM statement is scoped to SnO2/G-0.3. Figure 3 annotates d(110) = 0.34 nm in each sample panel. The predicted Bragg value 0.337 nm is reference interpretation, not a second measured lattice spacing. No unit-cell refinement or coordinates are supplied.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Figures 1–3 and results

intuition.title: More tin changes loading and morphology
intuition.text: TGA gives approximate SnO2 mass percentages of 63, 68 and 74%. The source attributes the slower increase in SnO2 fraction than tin charge to partial SnCl2 loss, without measuring a recovery balance. TEM indicates more oxide particles on smaller graphene sheets as tin charge increases; numerical sheet dimensions are unreported.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Morphology and TGA discussion

intuition.title: Spectral comparisons retain their scope
intuition.text: GO bands are assigned at 1401, 1735, 1220, 1052, 827 and 1620 cm−1. The source assigns the composite-series 606 cm−1 band to Sn–O and interprets loss of several oxygen-group bands as reduction. GO Raman G and D positions are 1591.3 and 1365.6 cm−1; composite D/G ratios are 1.13, 1.25 and 1.34. These ratios are not particle sizes. XPS binding energies are scoped to GO or the SnO2/G-0.3 comparison as stated.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, FTIR, Raman and XPS discussion

intuition.title: Electrode processing is a separate supporting route
intuition.text: Each composite is mixed with carbon black and PVDF at 80:15:5 by weight in NMP, doctor-bladed onto copper and vacuum-dried at 120 °C for 8 h. Cells use lithium foil, polypropylene separator and 1 M LiPF6 in EC/DMC (1:1 by weight), with overnight soaking. These steps support the electrochemical measurements and do not demonstrate new nanoparticle structures.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Section 2.3

intuition.title: Battery results are specimen-linked
intuition.text: At 200 mA/g between 0.01 and 1.5 V versus Li, reported reversible capacities are 541.3, 402.7 and 222.4 mAh/g. After 35 cycles, retentions are about 69.7, 34.2 and 33.6%; only the 0.3 specimen has a separately stated 35-cycle capacity, 377.3 mAh/g. The authors propose that larger graphene sheets and lower oxide coverage reduce pulverization and improve conduction. These mechanisms are interpretations, not directly measured stress or conductivity.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 4, Figure 7 and discussion

intuition.text: The introductory 782 mAh/g theoretical SnO2 capacity, literature bare-SnO2 performance and prospective sensor uses are background. No standalone pure SnO2 comparator synthesis is given here. All 33 bibliography entries are retained, but their full sources are unreviewed.

intuition.title: Three charges create three named composites
intuition.text: SnCl2·2H2O charges of 300, 600 and 1200 mg are paired with the same 100 mL aqueous GO input at 0.2 g/L. The products are SnO2/G-0.3, -0.6 and -1.2, respectively. All are stirred for 24 h at room temperature, collected, washed and dried at 100 °C. The GO preparation is cited rather than reproduced; this recipe starts from the supplied GO dispersion.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1, Section 2.1

intuition.title: Coupled redox is the authors’ interpretation
intuition.text: The authors interpret the process as Sn2+ oxidation coupled to GO deoxygenation, supported by SnO2 diffraction and changes in FTIR/XPS. The proposed transformation is not a balanced experimentally measured reaction equation. No unique oxygen content of GO or graphene, tin conversion yield or dissolved speciation is supplied.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–3, Preparation and structural/spectroscopic discussion

intuition.title: Size and structure describe different quantities
intuition.text: XRD gives tetragonal SnO2 and Scherrer domain sizes of 8.4, 7.8 and 8.4 nm for the three composites. The text’s less-than-10 nm TEM statement is scoped to SnO2/G-0.3. Figure 3 annotates d(110) = 0.34 nm in each sample panel. The predicted Bragg value 0.337 nm is reference interpretation, not a second measured lattice spacing. No unit-cell refinement or coordinates are supplied.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Figures 1–3 and results

intuition.title: More tin changes loading and morphology
intuition.text: TGA gives approximate SnO2 mass percentages of 63, 68 and 74%. The source attributes the slower increase in SnO2 fraction than tin charge to partial SnCl2 loss, without measuring a recovery balance. TEM indicates more oxide particles on smaller graphene sheets as tin charge increases; numerical sheet dimensions are unreported.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Morphology and TGA discussion

intuition.title: Spectral comparisons retain their scope
intuition.text: GO bands are assigned at 1401, 1735, 1220, 1052, 827 and 1620 cm−1. The source assigns the composite-series 606 cm−1 band to Sn–O and interprets loss of several oxygen-group bands as reduction. GO Raman G and D positions are 1591.3 and 1365.6 cm−1; composite D/G ratios are 1.13, 1.25 and 1.34. These ratios are not particle sizes. XPS binding energies are scoped to GO or the SnO2/G-0.3 comparison as stated.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, FTIR, Raman and XPS discussion

intuition.title: Electrode processing is a separate supporting route
intuition.text: Each composite is mixed with carbon black and PVDF at 80:15:5 by weight in NMP, doctor-bladed onto copper and vacuum-dried at 120 °C for 8 h. Cells use lithium foil, polypropylene separator and 1 M LiPF6 in EC/DMC (1:1 by weight), with overnight soaking. These steps support the electrochemical measurements and do not demonstrate new nanoparticle structures.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Section 2.3

intuition.title: Battery results are specimen-linked
intuition.text: At 200 mA/g between 0.01 and 1.5 V versus Li, reported reversible capacities are 541.3, 402.7 and 222.4 mAh/g. After 35 cycles, retentions are about 69.7, 34.2 and 33.6%; only the 0.3 specimen has a separately stated 35-cycle capacity, 377.3 mAh/g. The authors propose that larger graphene sheets and lower oxide coverage reduce pulverization and improve conduction. These mechanisms are interpretations, not directly measured stress or conductivity.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 4, Figure 7 and discussion

intuition.title: References and introductory values are not new product data
intuition.text: The introductory 782 mAh/g theoretical SnO2 capacity, literature bare-SnO2 performance and prospective sensor uses are background. No standalone pure SnO2 comparator synthesis is given here. All 33 bibliography entries are retained, but their full sources are unreviewed.

intuition.text: TGA gives approximate SnO2 mass percentages of 63, 68 and 74%. The source attributes the slower increase in SnO2 fraction than tin charge to partial SnCl2 loss, without measuring a recovery balance. TEM indicates more oxide particles on smaller graphene sheets as tin charge increases; numerical sheet dimensions are unreported.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Morphology and TGA discussion

intuition.title: Spectral comparisons retain their scope
intuition.text: GO bands are assigned at 1401, 1735, 1220, 1052, 827 and 1620 cm−1. The source assigns the composite-series 606 cm−1 band to Sn–O and interprets loss of several oxygen-group bands as reduction. GO Raman G and D positions are 1591.3 and 1365.6 cm−1; composite D/G ratios are 1.13, 1.25 and 1.34. These ratios are not particle sizes. XPS binding energies are scoped to GO or the SnO2/G-0.3 comparison as stated.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, FTIR, Raman and XPS discussion

intuition.title: Electrode processing is a separate supporting route
intuition.text: Each composite is mixed with carbon black and PVDF at 80:15:5 by weight in NMP, doctor-bladed onto copper and vacuum-dried at 120 °C for 8 h. Cells use lithium foil, polypropylene separator and 1 M LiPF6 in EC/DMC (1:1 by weight), with overnight soaking. These steps support the electrochemical measurements and do not demonstrate new nanoparticle structures.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Section 2.3

intuition.title: Battery results are specimen-linked
intuition.text: At 200 mA/g between 0.01 and 1.5 V versus Li, reported reversible capacities are 541.3, 402.7 and 222.4 mAh/g. After 35 cycles, retentions are about 69.7, 34.2 and 33.6%; only the 0.3 specimen has a separately stated 35-cycle capacity, 377.3 mAh/g. The authors propose that larger graphene sheets and lower oxide coverage reduce pulverization and improve conduction. These mechanisms are interpretations, not directly measured stress or conductivity.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 4, Figure 7 and discussion

intuition.title: References and introductory values are not new product data
intuition.text: The introductory 782 mAh/g theoretical SnO2 capacity, literature bare-SnO2 performance and prospective sensor uses are background. No standalone pure SnO2 comparator synthesis is given here. All 33 bibliography entries are retained, but their full sources are unreviewed.

bindings.source_locator: SI PDF p. 4–6, CdSe synthesis and cleaning
bindings.caption: Load TOPO and ODPA into a 50 mL three-neck flask with one-inch stirbar, thermocouple adaptor, reflux condenser and rubber septum. Stir vigorously under vacuum at 100 °C for at least 30 min. Equipment geometry is illustrative; exact source conditions are retained in the operation.

bindings.source_locator: SI PDF p. 5, CdSe synthesis
bindings.caption: Admit argon and heat to 275 °C. Bring out 1.065 g portions of each stock in sealed vials; protect the Cd vial with foil. Add only the explicitly stated 0.95 g Cd stock slowly dropwise with efficient mixing; gas evolution and foaming occur. Equipment geometry is illustrative; exact source conditions are retained in the operation.

bindings.source_locator: SI PDF p. 5, CdSe synthesis
bindings.caption: Equilibrate at 330 °C and rapidly inject the prepared selenium solution with vigorous stirring. The prepared selenium vial contains 1.065 g; no separate measured injection loss is supplied. Equipment geometry is illustrative; exact source conditions are retained in the operation.

bindings.source_locator: SI PDF p. 5, CdSe synthesis and parenthetical product values
bindings.caption: Lower to 315 °C and grow the size-linked sample for 7 min. The general procedure allows 7–10 min; this range is not a separate measured size series. Yellow color appears at about 2 min, then orange/red/brown. Equipment geometry is illustrative; exact source conditions are retained in the operation.

bindings.source_locator: SI PDF p. 5, Quench
bindings.caption: Submerge in a stirred room-temperature silicon oil bath (source wording). Begin cleaning once the mixture is below 100 °C; no cooling rate is reported. Equipment geometry is illustrative; exact source conditions are retained in the operation.

bindings.source_locator: SI PDF p. 6, Cleaning CdSe and CdSe/ZnS
bindings.caption: Below 100 °C dilute with dry degassed acetone to 50 mL total volume. Transfer under argon into the glovebox and centrifuge the milky suspension; speed and dwell are unspecified. Equipment geometry is illustrative; exact source conditions are retained in the operation.

bindings.source_locator: SI PDF p. 6, Cleaning CdSe and CdSe/ZnS
bindings.caption: Redissolve in 15 mL anhydrous chloroform, add 5 mL octylamine, then acetone to 50 mL total volume; immediately centrifuge to collect the nanocrystal film. Equipment geometry is illustrative; exact source conditions are retained in the operation.

bindings.source_locator: SI PDF p. 6, Cleaning CdSe and CdSe/ZnS
bindings.caption: Dissolve the film in 15 mL hexane. Add acetone slowly until precipitation, shake/sonicate to redissolve, and repeat dropwise until the solid no longer clears. Discard this solid and retain the colored supernatant. Equipment geometry is illustrative; exact source conditions are retained in the operation.

bindings.source_locator: SI PDF p. 6, Cleaning CdSe and CdSe/ZnS
bindings.caption: Add further acetone to the colored supernatant to precipitate nanocrystals. Repeat the hexane/acetone fractional-precipitation step a second time. Unreported antisolvent volumes and centrifugation settings remain unknown. Equipment geometry is illustrative; exact source conditions are retained in the operation.

bindings.source_locator: SI PDF p. 6, Cleaning CdSe and CdSe/ZnS
bindings.caption: Vacuum-dry away volatile impurities; redissolve an analytical portion in d8-toluene for NMR. AuNPs and peptide are mixed at a nominal 1:150 molar ratio, stirred for 10 h at room temperature, centrifuged and redispersed. The authors interpret the FTIR and gel changes as peptide attachment through Au–S bonding; no surface coverage or atomistic conformation is measured.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Modification of AuNPs and Figure 2

intuition.title: Cleavage and inner-filter interpretation
intuition.text: The authors propose removal of the negatively charged DDDEVD segment by caspase-3, leaving GRRRR-Mpa on gold and promoting electrostatic aggregation. They attribute fluorescence recovery to reduced spectral overlap as gold absorption shifts from 520 to 680 nm. This mechanism is their interpretation. Main statements of negative zeta potential refer to excluded Figure S3; no zeta magnitudes are supplied here.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–3, Scheme 1, mechanism and IFE discussion

intuition.title: Keep concentration and ratio discrepancies visible
intuition.text: Figure 3 lists Au-Ps concentrations on a 10−9 M scale and CdTe at 1.14 × 10−8 M, but its nominal Au-Ps:CdTe ratio list behaves as though the concentrations were comparable. The fluorescent-assay Methods also say 1:1, while Figure 5 labels about a tenfold concentration difference. No exponent, ratio, dilution or aliquot is silently repaired.

intuition.title: Assay properties are not synthesis outputs
intuition.text: The main reports a 27.68–129.15 pM linear range and an 18 pM detection limit. Figure 5C annotates Y = 0.0039X + 1.0376 and R² = 0.9967. These describe the fluorescent assay, not particle morphology or separate materials syntheses. Bars and curve points are not digitized.

intuition.title: Three material protocols, separate assay contexts
intuition.text: The main supplies aqueous GSH-capped CdTe synthesis, citrate reduction of gold and subsequent peptide modification of the gold colloid. The mixed Au-Ps/CdTe optical assays are nonconjugated probe mixtures, not a new Au–CdTe composite synthesis. Supporting assay series retain their own aliquots, concentrations and unknown specimen links.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–3, Scheme 1 and Materials and Methods

intuition.title: CdTe morphology remains missing
intuition.text: The main gives NaBH4/Te precursor preparation, CdCl2–GSH stock, pH 9.0, 400 µL/0.8 µL aliquots and 100 °C for 30 min. It directs TEM characterization to Figure S1, which lies in excluded SI. The 520 nm fluorescence maximum and estimated particle concentration do not establish a CdTe diameter, shape or crystal phase.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Synthesis of CdTe QDs and Figure 1b

intuition.title: Gold TEM belongs to peptide-modified gold
intuition.text: Citrate-stabilized gold is prepared by adding 1.6 mL of 1% citrate to 50 mL of 0.25 mM HAuCl4 at boiling, followed by 10 min at boiling and 4 °C storage. Main Figure 4B and the about-18 nm average explicitly concern Au-Ps after peptide modification. Figure 4C shows enzyme-induced aggregation without a named caspase dose. Neither panel is a CdTe micrograph.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–4, Au synthesis, Results and Figure 4B–C

intuition.title: Thiol-peptide modification is source-reported
intuition.text: The peptide stock is 2 mM DK (Mpa)-12 in phosphate buffer at pH 7.4. AuNPs and peptide are mixed at a nominal 1:150 molar ratio, stirred for 10 h at room temperature, centrifuged and redispersed. The authors interpret the FTIR and gel changes as peptide attachment through Au–S bonding; no surface coverage or atomistic conformation is measured.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Modification of AuNPs and Figure 2

intuition.title: Cleavage and inner-filter interpretation
intuition.text: The authors propose removal of the negatively charged DDDEVD segment by caspase-3, leaving GRRRR-Mpa on gold and promoting electrostatic aggregation. They attribute fluorescence recovery to reduced spectral overlap as gold absorption shifts from 520 to 680 nm. This mechanism is their interpretation. Main statements of negative zeta potential refer to excluded Figure S3; no zeta magnitudes are supplied here.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–3, Scheme 1, mechanism and IFE discussion

intuition.title: Keep concentration and ratio discrepancies visible
intuition.text: Figure 3 lists Au-Ps concentrations on a 10−9 M scale and CdTe at 1.14 × 10−8 M, but its nominal Au-Ps:CdTe ratio list behaves as though the concentrations were comparable. The fluorescent-assay Methods also say 1:1, while Figure 5 labels about a tenfold concentration difference. No exponent, ratio, dilution or aliquot is silently repaired.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–4, Assay Methods and Figures 3–5

intuition.title: Assay properties are not synthesis outputs
intuition.text: The main reports a 27.68–129.15 pM linear range and an 18 pM detection limit. Figure 5C annotates Y = 0.0039X + 1.0376 and R² = 0.9967. These describe the fluorescent assay, not particle morphology or separate materials syntheses. Bars and curve points are not digitized.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 4–5, Figure 5 and Conclusions

intuition.title: Why vary feed ratio, temperature and reaction time
intuition.summary: The authors compare metal:Te feed ratio, temperature and duration to study nonstoichiometric telluride phases. They report no obvious difference from Cu:Te 2:1 to 1.5:1 at otherwise unchanged 160 °C/8 h conditions. At lower ratios they describe orthorhombic Cu2.86Te2 and other phases. They propose that hydrazine reduction of metal ions to elemental metal at room temperature may leave reactants unevenly dispersed, contributing to phase diversity. This is the authors' qualitative explanation, not an established mechanism; 1.5:1 is prose context, not a separate tabulated route.
intuition.scope: Source discussion; distinction between tabulated experimental rows and author interpretation is retained.

kudryavtseva1997-sno2-a702862h-a-as-prep.summary: Dissolve the stated but unquantified precursor charge in deionized water in an ice bath. The bath temperature is not numerically reported. Slowly add ammonia to the stirred solution until alpha-stannic-acid precipitation is complete. Preserve the prose/Figure 1 formulation ambiguity. Centrifuge and wash with deionized water until the AgNO3 test indicates no chloride. The analytical test does not imply adding AgNO3 to the retained bulk precipitate. Dry the washed precipitate. Drying atmosphere is not specified.

intuition.title: Why combine these colloids?
intuition.text: The authors pursued binary order as a route to controlled placement and stoichiometry in future nanocrystalline solids. They cite Ag⁺ as a p-type dopant in bulk PbTe; the assembly itself does not prove atomic doping.

intuition.title: Why tune sizes and ligands?
intuition.text: The authors identify relative size and monodispersity as factors for ordered assembly. They add charged amphiphilic ligand in some preparations to narrow charge-state spread, but did not independently verify the charge distributions or assign each Figure 3 specimen to a specific additive branch.

intuition.title: Why combine these colloids?
intuition.text: The authors pursued binary order as a route to controlled placement and stoichiometry in future nanocrystalline solids. They cite Ag⁺ as a p-type dopant in bulk PbTe; the assembly itself does not prove atomic doping.

intuition.title: Why tune sizes and ligands?
intuition.text: The authors identify relative size and monodispersity as factors for ordered assembly. They add charged amphiphilic ligand in some preparations to narrow charge-state spread, but did not independently verify the charge distributions or assign each Figure 3 specimen to a specific additive branch.

intuition.title: Solvent and assembly
intuition.text: The reported Method 1 hexane and toluene branches produce distinct superlattice sizes and orientations; keep their product samples separate.

intuition.title: Free triphenylphosphine
intuition.text: Acetone-washed and PPh3-readded branches differ in observed film versus faceted superlattice outcomes. Figure 9 also changes deposition method, so it is not an isolated PPh3 effect.

intuition.title: What the model contributes
intuition.text: Figure 8 presents calculated interaction potentials. Its curves do not establish a measured sample structure or a source-reported atomic coordinate set.

conflictPairs.text: Main PDF p.3 explicitly says 15-min mixing at room temperature and p.7 says 45-min reduction at room temperature; main-referred SI PDF p.1 Figure S1 marks heating (Δ) during both steps. Both reports are retained without selecting a reactor setpoint.

Figure 2 has three incompatible panel attributions: visible labels show (d) size and (e) SAED; p.4 body and caption call the size histogram (e), with caption assigning SAED to (d); p.5 body calls SAED (e). The visible panels support d=size/e=SAED, without treating the body as uniform.
Main PDF p.5 body assigns the ~32.57° XRD peak to (112), while Figure 3 plot/caption labels (122).

Main PDF p.7 body attributes Figure 6c to changing CQD concentration and a steady intensity decrease; Figure 6 caption calls it varying AgNO3 amount, the legend has only 50/100/200/400 µL, and plotted intensity is nonmonotonic. No dose–response or reagent assignment is inferred.

conflictPairs.text: Main p.3 direct comparison says 24, 31 and 38 nm shells give stronger fluorescence than free QDs; later same-page wording says enhancement at shell thickness >24 nm. The 24 nm measured comparison is retained without deriving a strict threshold.

Main p.2 says Ag/SiO2 was centrifuged and washed, whereas p.3 explicitly says the later Ag/SiO2-QD optical dispersions were not collected/washed to remove excess QDs. These workups apply to different stages and are not merged.

conflictPairs.text: Main p.2 says PVP-H does not produce well-defined nanoparticles even at low injection rates while the explicit PVP-H protocol produces defined nanorods. We interpret the comparison narrowly as failure to produce the AgNH-type particles, not as a negation of the rod result.

Main p.7 states 2–3 weeks of open-air Ag rod exposure; SI Figure S2 reports the pictured Ag2S nanotube after 3 weeks. The SI caption explicitly says panel a Ag rod and panel b nanotube are typical different objects.

source_contexts.statement: AgNS extinction fitted by Gaussian (R²=0.972) and Lorentzian (R²=0.997) curves; these are source fit qualities, not particle-size measurements.
Reactant Ag nanoparticle solution spectra right after synthesis and after one month at ambient room temperature; distinct from SI p.1 optional 4 °C pre-etch storage.

source_contexts.locator: SI PDF p.4, Figure S5a–c; main PDF p.5
source_contexts.statement: Before/after Ag surface XPS supports oxidized surface states; pre-etch PXRD is dominated by fcc Ag. Do not claim bulk Ag2O, oxide thickness, or identity of individual imaged particles.
Precipitate Cu 2p3/2 XPS is assigned to CuO, distinct from Cu, Cu2O, and CuCl2; precipitate is not the AgNS surface.

Cu(II)-mediated etching rounds Ag particles within 15 min in a kinetic comparison (three repeats); standard synthesis reaction still runs 2 h. Conventional comparison exceeds 3 h; panel b shows a 250 nm ascorbic-acid-associated peak.

conflictPairs.text: Main p.2 reports 67% AgNC and 33% right bipyramid after flocculation; SI Figure S1c labels 66.98% and 32.02%, which sum to 99.00%. Preserve source statements without normalization.
SI Figure S10 caption describes green (c) and red (d) PL distributions, but the artwork labels these panels b and c; sample links follow visible panels and note the caption error.

bindings.source_locator: SI PDF p.1, Synthesis of silver nanospheres, seed paragraph
bindings.caption: MatterSyn-authored apparatus schematic. A 20 mL glass vial is stirred during CTAC preheat and sequential AgNO3/NaBH4 additions; the 2–3 nm seed range is reported, not a drawn scale.

bindings.source_locator: SI PDF p.1, Synthesis of silver nanospheres, growth paragraph
bindings.caption: MatterSyn-authored apparatus schematic. The capped 20 mL glass vial shows the sequential seed/AgTFA addition and later ascorbic-acid growth phase; the cap is source-reported.

bindings.source_locator: SI PDF p.1, Synthesis of silver nanospheres, selective flocculation
bindings.caption: MatterSyn-authored apparatus schematic. BDAC-treated capped vial rests undisturbed in a 30 °C oven after removal of the stir bar; rod/wire flocculate is separated from supernatant.

bindings.source_locator: SI PDF p.1, Synthesis of silver nanospheres, post-flocculation wash
bindings.caption: MatterSyn-authored apparatus schematic. The selected supernatant, rather than the rod/wire flocculate, is transferred to a 50 mL centrifuge tube for two spins and redispersion.

bindings.source_locator: SI PDF pp.1–2, Synthesis of silver nanospheres, oxidative etching; main PDF pp.2–5, Figures 1–4
bindings.caption: MatterSyn-authored apparatus schematic. The standard branch uses a 20 mL glass vial, 60 °C preheat and Cu(II) addition; no sealed or inert etch atmosphere is implied.

bindings.source_locator: SI PDF p.2, Synthesis of silver nanospheres, ligand exchange and workup
bindings.caption: MatterSyn-authored apparatus schematic. SDS/PVP addition precedes the 0.2 µm syringe membrane filter; the filtered sample moves to a 50 mL tube for centrifugation and redispersion.

bindings.source_locator: SI PDF p.2, Mechanistic study for oxidative etching; main PDF p.4, Figure 4b
bindings.caption: MatterSyn-authored apparatus schematic. Ag and Cu(II) feeds undergo ten cycles of 1 min vacuum sonication followed by argon replenishment, then react under argon; exact inherited aliquots are omitted.

bindings.source_locator: SI PDF p.2, Mechanistic study for oxidative etching; main PDF p.4, Figure 4b
bindings.caption: MatterSyn-authored apparatus schematic. The Cu(I) negative control uses an acetonitrile/water mixture because Cu(I) is not soluble in water; precursor, ratio and dose are unreported.

bindings.source_locator: SI PDF p.2, Mechanistic study for oxidative etching, polysorbate 20 exchange
bindings.caption: MatterSyn-authored apparatus schematic. After flocculation, the supernatant is centrifuged four times with two 1 wt% and two 0.1 wt% Tween 20 redispersions; spin settings are not reported.

bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.4, Figure 4b; p.5, chloride-control Results
bindings.caption: MatterSyn-authored apparatus schematic. A source-scoped generic reaction-mixture drawing represents Tween-exchanged Ag and Cu(II), without copying standard CTAC, Cu aliquot, temperature or time.

bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.6, size-control paragraph; SI PDF p.6, Figure S8
bindings.caption: MatterSyn-authored apparatus schematic. This comparative dose schematic separates the source-labeled Cu(II) additions and observed size trend without assigning unreported common conditions or dose–diameter pairs.

bindings.source_locator: SI PDF p.6, Figure S8b, 460 µL addition label
bindings.caption: MatterSyn-authored apparatus schematic. The 460 µL Cu(II) addition is source-labeled for this variant; vessel, concentration and other reaction conditions are not assigned from the 380 µL standard branch.

bindings.source_locator: SI PDF p.6, Figure S8b, 580 µL addition label
bindings.caption: MatterSyn-authored apparatus schematic. The 580 µL Cu(II) addition is source-labeled for this variant; vessel, concentration and other reaction conditions are not assigned from the 380 µL standard branch.

bindings.source_locator: SI PDF p.2, Fabrication of monodisperse Ag nanosphere film; main PDF p.6, film Results
bindings.caption: MatterSyn-authored apparatus schematic. The ITO glass substrate holds a 9 mm × 1.8 mm sticky chamber for 200 µL PVP-AgNS dispersion (OD 80 at 1 cm); drying and wash steps are source-reported.

bindings.source_locator: SI PDF p.2, Film fabrication; main PDF p.6, QD-film preparation
bindings.caption: MatterSyn-authored apparatus schematic. Green QD solution is spin-coated on the AgNS/ITO film; QD preparation follows prior reports, and coating speed/time/volume are not supplied.

bindings.source_locator: SI PDF p.2, Film fabrication; main PDF p.6, QD-film preparation
bindings.caption: MatterSyn-authored apparatus schematic. Red QD solution is spin-coated on the AgNS/ITO film; QD preparation follows prior reports, and coating speed/time/volume are not supplied.

bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.6, bare-QD comparison; SI PDF p.8, Figure S13
bindings.caption: MatterSyn-authored apparatus schematic. Green and red QD reference films are shown on bare ITO without AgNSs; control-specific spin conditions are not reported.

bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.6, unetched AgNP film comparison; SI PDF p.7, Figure S12
bindings.caption: MatterSyn-authored apparatus schematic. The control uses AgNP solution before oxidative etching for a film compared with green-QD optical variation; its preparation settings are not inherited from AgNS film.

conflictPairs.text: Main Figure 4 stopped-flow caption says 6.67 mM AgClO4 before 1:1 mixing; Figure 5 says 6.66 mM. Both captions are retained; common 3.33 mM post-mix value is approximate.

Main p.4 body says both microfluidic XAS and stopped-flow observe exchange in 3.33 mM Ag+, whereas Figure 4 assigns the microfluidic trace 5 mM AgClO4 before side-stream mixing. Side-stream diffusion prevents a simple 1:1 chip dilution assignment; preserve both statements without merging conditions.
SI Figure S2 phase sample is 2.8 mM CdSe/5 mM AgClO4 chip reacted; main Figure 3 XAS uses 1.4/5 mM, so its tetragonal phase cannot be assigned to the same physical aliquot.

bindings.caption: Measure initial absorbance at 281.5 nm and dilute a separate aliquot until A281.5=2.6. Exact dilution and mixing aliquots unreported. Use normalized samples for the QD array; base-dependent concentrations given in Figure S10. Retain the initial absorbance for later Beer-Lambert calculation. Abstract process symbol; vessel geometry and unreported conditions are not inferred.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.6 / printed881, Identification of the Sample at Varying Concentration; SI p.6 FigureS10

bindings.caption: Use each normalized analyte separately with MA-QDs. Modified-method exact well volumes are unreported; do not impose standard 190+10 uL aliquots. Conceptual 96-well plate; separate targets and ligands are separate well contexts, not mixed together.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.6 / printed881, Identification of the Sample at Varying Concentration; SI p.6 FigureS10

bindings.caption: Incubate for 60 min at room temperature before fluorescence recording. This follows the general pattern-sensing method; duration is not independently repeated in this modified-context section. Conceptual 96-well plate; separate targets and ligands are separate well contexts, not mixed together.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.6 / printed881, Identification of the Sample at Varying Concentration; SI p.6 FigureS10

bindings.caption: Record 600 nm emission with 480 nm excitation on Tecan Infinite M1000. Repeat each target six times. Combine this ligand response with the other three ligands in SPSS 11 LDA; six replicates are analytical repeats. Conceptual 96-well plate; separate targets and ligands are separate well contexts, not mixed together.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.6 / printed881, Identification of the Sample at Varying Concentration; SI p.6 FigureS10

bindings.caption: Classify the four-ligand response pattern by LDA, then determine initial concentration from initial A281.5 and the identified base molar extinction coefficient using Beer-Lambert law. Figure S9 plots coefficients; exact numerical coefficients are not tabulated and are not digitized. Abstract process symbol; vessel geometry and unreported conditions are not inferred.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.6 / printed881, Identification of the Sample at Varying Concentration

bindings.caption: Measure initial absorbance at 281.5 nm and dilute a separate aliquot until A281.5=2.6. Exact dilution and mixing aliquots unreported. Use normalized samples for the QD array; base-dependent concentrations given in Figure S10. Retain the initial absorbance for later Beer-Lambert calculation. Abstract process symbol; vessel geometry and unreported conditions are not inferred.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.6 / printed881, Identification of the Sample at Varying Concentration; SI p.6 FigureS10

bindings.caption: Use each normalized analyte separately with NAC-QDs. Modified-method exact well volumes are unreported; do not impose standard 190+10 uL aliquots. Conceptual 96-well plate; separate targets and ligands are separate well contexts, not mixed together.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.6 / printed881, Identification of the Sample at Varying Concentration; SI p.6 FigureS10

bindings.caption: Incubate for 60 min at room temperature before fluorescence recording. This follows the general pattern-sensing method; duration is not independently repeated in this modified-context section. Conceptual 96-well plate; separate targets and ligands are separate well contexts, not mixed together.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.6 / printed881, Identification of the Sample at Varying Concentration; SI p.6 FigureS10

bindings.caption: Record 600 nm emission with 480 nm excitation on Tecan Infinite M1000. Repeat each target six times. Combine this ligand response with the other three ligands in SPSS 11 LDA; six replicates are analytical repeats. Conceptual 96-well plate; separate targets and ligands are separate well contexts, not mixed together.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.6 / printed881, Identification of the Sample at Varying Concentration; SI p.6 FigureS10

bindings.caption: Classify the four-ligand response pattern by LDA, then determine initial concentration from initial A281.5 and the identified base molar extinction coefficient using Beer-Lambert law. Figure S9 plots coefficients; exact numerical coefficients are not tabulated and are not digitized. Abstract process symbol; vessel geometry and unreported conditions are not inferred.

bindings.caption: Measure initial absorbance at 281.5 nm and dilute a separate aliquot until A281.5=2.6. Exact dilution and mixing aliquots unreported. Use normalized samples for the QD array; base-dependent concentrations given in Figure S10. Retain the initial absorbance for later Beer-Lambert calculation. Abstract process symbol; vessel geometry and unreported conditions are not inferred.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.6 / printed881, Identification of the Sample at Varying Concentration; SI p.6 FigureS10

bindings.caption: Use each normalized analyte separately with TGA-QDs. Modified-method exact well volumes are unreported; do not impose standard 190+10 uL aliquots. Conceptual 96-well plate; separate targets and ligands are separate well contexts, not mixed together.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.6 / printed881, Identification of the Sample at Varying Concentration; SI p.6 FigureS10

bindings.caption: Incubate for 60 min at room temperature before fluorescence recording. This follows the general pattern-sensing method; duration is not independently repeated in this modified-context section. Conceptual 96-well plate; separate targets and ligands are separate well contexts, not mixed together.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.6 / printed881, Identification of the Sample at Varying Concentration; SI p.6 FigureS10

bindings.caption: Record 600 nm emission with 480 nm excitation on Tecan Infinite M1000. Repeat each target six times. Combine this ligand response with the other three ligands in SPSS 11 LDA; six replicates are analytical repeats. Conceptual 96-well plate; separate targets and ligands are separate well contexts, not mixed together.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.6 / printed881, Identification of the Sample at Varying Concentration; SI p.6 FigureS10

bindings.caption: Classify the four-ligand response pattern by LDA, then determine initial concentration from initial A281.5 and the identified base molar extinction coefficient using Beer-Lambert law. Figure S9 plots coefficients; exact numerical coefficients are not tabulated and are not digitized. Abstract process symbol; vessel geometry and unreported conditions are not inferred.

figures.title: Running-solution volume series
figures.summary: 10, 15 and20 µL operating volumes, five scans; this is measurement-solution volume, not CdS coating volume. ECL increased when running-solution volume rose from 10 to 15 µL and decreased slightly at 20 µL. The authors identify 15 µL as optimal for a thin-layer cell 1.10 cm long and 0.74 cm wide. At lower volume the solution did not cover the entire hydrophilic paper area. The authors propose that extra solution leaking outside the thin-layer electrochemical cell explains the change in ECL with increasing electrolyte volume. Leakage is a proposed explanation; its volume is not measured here.

bindings.caption: Combine 0.3 mmol InCl3, no EDTA, and 5 mL anhydrous oleylamine in a 50 mL three-neck flask. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, General Considerations and Synthesis of InP Quantum Dots

bindings.caption: Hold the precursor mixture under vacuum at 120 °C for 1 h. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, General Considerations and Synthesis of InP Quantum Dots

bindings.caption: Replace vacuum with an inert atmosphere and heat to 180 °C. Nitrogen glovebox or Schlenk handling is stated generally. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, General Considerations and Synthesis of InP Quantum Dots

bindings.caption: Rapidly inject 0.33 mL (1.2 mmol) tris(diethylamino)phosphine. Exact injection duration is unreported. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, General Considerations and Synthesis of InP Quantum Dots

bindings.caption: Monitor until the absorption spectrum is constant; reported after 120 min. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, General Considerations and Synthesis of InP Quantum Dots

bindings.caption: Dilute 20 µL reaction aliquots in 2 mL HPLC-grade toluene for Cary 5000 UV–visible monitoring. Exact aliquot identities and optical path length are unreported. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, General Considerations and Synthesis of InP Quantum Dots

bindings.caption: Cool the reaction mixture to room temperature and move it into a nitrogen glovebox. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, General Considerations and Synthesis of InP Quantum Dots

bindings.caption: Precipitate the product with anhydrous methanol; volume is unreported. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, General Considerations and Synthesis of InP Quantum Dots

bindings.caption: Centrifuge at 7830 rpm for 10 min. Rotor radius and relative centrifugal force are unreported. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, General Considerations and Synthesis of InP Quantum Dots

bindings.caption: Redisperse in toluene. The source says this procedure was repeated 3 times; it does not clarify whether the initial cycle is included in that count. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, General Considerations and Synthesis of InP Quantum Dots

bindings.caption: Dropcast 5 µL dilute QD/toluene solution on the specified carbon/copper grid. Dry for 10 min, then under vacuum overnight. Exact dilution and drying temperature are unreported. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, Characterization

bindings.caption: Use FEI Tecnai G2 F20 SuperTwin at 200 kV in bright-field mode. Manually measure more than 300 particles with ImageJ from at least two grid locations. Low contrast may inflate the distribution width. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, Characterization; Main PDF pp.2–3 / printed 6153–6154, Figure 1 and size/phase discussion; SI pp.3–5, Figures S2–S4

bindings.caption: Dropcast the purified sample as a solid film on a silicon wafer; measure on a Bruker D8 Discover. Film loading is unreported. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, Characterization

bindings.caption: Measure in toluene-d8 using the 500 MHz Bruker Advance instrument at 298 K. Use 10 scans, 2 dummy scans and a 30 s relaxation delay for QD samples. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, Characterization; SI p.6 Figure S5

bindings.caption: Combine 0.3 mmol InCl3, 0.25 equivalent EDTA and 5 mL anhydrous oleylamine in a 50 mL three-neck flask. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, General Considerations and Synthesis of InP Quantum Dots

bindings.caption: Hold the precursor mixture under vacuum at 120 °C for 1 h. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, General Considerations and Synthesis of InP Quantum Dots

bindings.caption: Replace vacuum with an inert atmosphere and heat to 180 °C. Nitrogen glovebox or Schlenk handling is stated generally. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, General Considerations and Synthesis of InP Quantum Dots

bindings.caption: Rapidly inject 0.33 mL (1.2 mmol) tris(diethylamino)phosphine. Exact injection duration is unreported. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, General Considerations and Synthesis of InP Quantum Dots

bindings.caption: Monitor until the absorption spectrum is constant; reported after 120 min. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, General Considerations and Synthesis of InP Quantum Dots

bindings.caption: Dilute 20 µL reaction aliquots in 2 mL HPLC-grade toluene for Cary 5000 UV–visible monitoring. Exact aliquot identities and optical path length are unreported. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, General Considerations and Synthesis of InP Quantum Dots

bindings.caption: Cool the reaction mixture to room temperature and move it into a nitrogen glovebox. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, General Considerations and Synthesis of InP Quantum Dots

bindings.caption: Precipitate the product with anhydrous methanol; volume is unreported. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, General Considerations and Synthesis of InP Quantum Dots

bindings.caption: Centrifuge at 7830 rpm for 10 min. Rotor radius and relative centrifugal force are unreported. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, General Considerations and Synthesis of InP Quantum Dots

bindings.caption: Redisperse in toluene. The source says this procedure was repeated 3 times; it does not clarify whether the initial cycle is included in that count. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, General Considerations and Synthesis of InP Quantum Dots

bindings.caption: Dropcast 5 µL dilute QD/toluene solution on the specified carbon/copper grid. Dry for 10 min, then under vacuum overnight. Exact dilution and drying temperature are unreported. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, Characterization

bindings.caption: Use FEI Tecnai G2 F20 SuperTwin at 200 kV in bright-field mode. Manually measure more than 300 particles with ImageJ from at least two grid locations. Low contrast may inflate the distribution width. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, Characterization; Main PDF pp.2–3 / printed 6153–6154, Figure 1 and size/phase discussion; SI pp.3–5, Figures S2–S4

bindings.caption: Dropcast the purified sample as a solid film on a silicon wafer; measure on a Bruker D8 Discover. Film loading is unreported. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, Characterization

bindings.caption: Measure in toluene-d8 using the 500 MHz Bruker Advance instrument at 298 K. Use 10 scans, 2 dummy scans and a 30 s relaxation delay for QD samples. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, Characterization; SI p.6 Figure S5

bindings.caption: Use the source overnight crude-reaction 31P NMR context. The spectrum is recorded on the 500 MHz instrument at 298 K, with 135 scans and a 2 s delay. The source does not identify a solvent or aliquot volume for Figure S11; the benzene-d6 specification of Figure 5 is not transferred. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: SI p.11 Figure S11; main p.7 Characterization

bindings.caption: Combine 0.3 mmol InCl3, 0.5 equivalent EDTA and 5 mL anhydrous oleylamine in a 50 mL three-neck flask. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, General Considerations and Synthesis of InP Quantum Dots

bindings.caption: Hold the precursor mixture under vacuum at 120 °C for 1 h. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, General Considerations and Synthesis of InP Quantum Dots

bindings.caption: Replace vacuum with an inert atmosphere and heat to 180 °C. Nitrogen glovebox or Schlenk handling is stated generally. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, General Considerations and Synthesis of InP Quantum Dots

bindings.caption: Rapidly inject 0.33 mL (1.2 mmol) tris(diethylamino)phosphine. Exact injection duration is unreported. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, General Considerations and Synthesis of InP Quantum Dots

bindings.caption: Monitor until the absorption spectrum is constant; reported after 120 min. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, General Considerations and Synthesis of InP Quantum Dots

bindings.caption: Dilute 20 µL reaction aliquots in 2 mL HPLC-grade toluene for Cary 5000 UV–visible monitoring. Exact aliquot identities and optical path length are unreported. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, General Considerations and Synthesis of InP Quantum Dots

bindings.caption: Cool the reaction mixture to room temperature and move it into a nitrogen glovebox. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, General Considerations and Synthesis of InP Quantum Dots

bindings.caption: Precipitate the product with anhydrous methanol; volume is unreported. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, General Considerations and Synthesis of InP Quantum Dots

bindings.caption: Centrifuge at 7830 rpm for 10 min. Rotor radius and relative centrifugal force are unreported. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, General Considerations and Synthesis of InP Quantum Dots

bindings.caption: Redisperse in toluene. The source says this procedure was repeated 3 times; it does not clarify whether the initial cycle is included in that count. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, General Considerations and Synthesis of InP Quantum Dots

bindings.caption: Dropcast 5 µL dilute QD/toluene solution on the specified carbon/copper grid. Dry for 10 min, then under vacuum overnight. Exact dilution and drying temperature are unreported. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, Characterization

bindings.caption: Use FEI Tecnai G2 F20 SuperTwin at 200 kV in bright-field mode. Manually measure more than 300 particles with ImageJ from at least two grid locations. Low contrast may inflate the distribution width. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.

facts.label: Active phosphorus precursor consumption
facts.value: The source reports that active transaminated aminophosphine signals near 112/98 ppm disappear over the first approximately 10 min. Signals near 14/11 ppm persist in Figure 5 and are assigned to tautomers of the active transaminated precursor. The 30 ppm signal is phosphonium salt; the 18 ppm signal is proposed aminophosphine oxide.

source_locator.locator: Main p.5 Figure 5; p.7 Characterization

facts.label: Source yield normalization
facts.value: Raw yield estimates can exceed 100% for 0 and 0.25 equivalent EDTA because of optical/volume assumptions, organic absorption and scattering. Main plots normalize the maximum to 100%; this is not an absolute conversion or isolated mass yield.

source_locator.locator: SI p.18; main pp.3–4 Figure 2

facts.label: EDTA loading effect on growth and yield
facts.value: Across the EDTA series, higher EDTA decreases initial InP growth rates and relative optical yield; unprinted graph values remain source images.

source_locator.locator: Main pp.3–4 Figure 2 and rate discussion

conflictPairs.topic: Optical transition estimates for 0.75 equivalent EDTA
conflictPairs.context: Both estimates concern the 0.75 equivalent EDTA chloride synthesis and are Tauc-based. The main text reports 393 nm and directs the reader to the SI method, while the SI plot is annotated 3.14 eV = 395 nm. The source does not explain this numerical discrepancy; neither value is replaced, averaged or recalculated.

claims.label: Main-text LEET
claims.statement: The main text estimates the lowest-energy electronic transition using a Tauc plot as 393 nm and refers to the SI method; 393 nm is repeated in the particle-size model discussion.

claims.label: SI Tauc annotation

conflictPairs.topic: Early phosphorus-precursor depletion and persistent tautomers
conflictPairs.context: Only the 0.75 equivalent EDTA chloride reaction in Figure 5. The prose can imply that both active precursor and tautomers disappear near 10 min, while the plot retains tautomer signals later. Early active-precursor depletion does not establish disappearance of every phosphorus signal.

claims.label: Main-text wording
claims.statement: The text describes active transaminated aminophosphine disappearing over early time points near 10 min, and also mentions disappearance of the 14 and 11 ppm tautomer species as they convert back to the active precursor.

claims.label: Figure 5 observations

conflictPairs.topic: Optical transition estimates for 0.75 equivalent EDTA
conflictPairs.context: Both estimates concern the 0.75 equivalent EDTA chloride synthesis and are Tauc-based. The main text reports 393 nm and directs the reader to the SI method, while the SI plot is annotated 3.14 eV = 395 nm. The source does not explain this numerical discrepancy; neither value is replaced, averaged or recalculated.
